articles.title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf lost $3 million on $23 million Tiburon mansion after four years of searching for a buyer
articles.summary: In 2006, tennis legends Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf made a costly decision involving one of their most impressive real estate assets.
articles.body: In 2006, tennis legends Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf made a costly decision involving one of their most impressive real estate assets. After nearly four years on the market, the couple finally found a buyer for their sprawling Tiburon estate in California. The property attracted attention for its breathtaking views, luxury features and celebrity connections. Yet the final sale price came in below what Agassi had paid five years earlier. The deal showed that even a high-end property in a sought-after location can struggle to find the right buyer when its upkeep and price become difficult to justify.Andre Agassi's Tiburon estate took years to sellAndre Agassi and Steffi Graf agreed to sell the 3.5-acre estate for $20 million, around $3 million less than the $23 million Agassi reportedly paid in 2001. The sale was expected to close in the first week of January 2007, according to Bill Bullock, whose firm represented the couple.The property offered plenty of space and privacy. It featured a 10,500-square-foot main house, separate staff quarters measuring 2,500 square feet, two swimming pools, a stream and a tennis court. Its elevated setting also provided views of the Golden Gate Bridge and the San Francisco skyline.However, the estate's size came with significant carrying costs. Agassi's family rarely used the property, and his financial advisers wanted him to sell it rather than continue paying to maintain a largely vacant home.The original asking price stood at $24.5 million. After several reductions, Agassi lowered it to $21 million about six months before the reported deal. Bullock explained why the couple became more flexible on price."When they considered the annual cost of that property to sit there vacant, they decided that they needed a little inducement for the marketplace and they started reducing the price,"The final $20 million offer still ranked among the Bay Area's most expensive home sales that year. Stuart Peterson, president of hedge fund Artis Capital Management, agreed to buy the estate. His fund had also been a major investor in YouTube before Google's $1.65 billion acquisition of the video-sharing company.Why the luxury home struggled to attract buyersDespite its impressive setting, the Tiburon property had a drawback. Built in 1976, the house had not received a major renovation since the mid-1990s. That left parts of the estate feeling dated to prospective buyers, making it harder to compete in the luxury market.Bullock said several wealthy visitors, including movie stars, had toured the home but ultimately passed on it. The buyer planned to make changes, although details were not disclosed before the transaction closed.Agassi had wanted the property for years. He first considered buying it in the mid-1990s while married to actress Brooke Shields, but she disliked the compound and discouraged the purchase. When it returned to the market, Agassi acted quickly rather than risk losing it again.By 2006, Agassi had retired from professional tennis and was living in Las Vegas with Graf and their two children. The couple were also exploring property development, including a luxury condo-hotel project in Idaho. articles.title: Dana White bought three neighboring Las Vegas mansions for $6.2 million; after bulldozing them in Summerlin, he built a $50 million custom megacompound
articles.summary: UFC CEO Dana White bought three neighboring mansions in Las Vegas for a combined $6.2 million between October 2016 and March 2017.
articles.body: UFC CEO Dana White bought three neighboring mansions in Las Vegas for a combined $6.2 million between October 2016 and March 2017. The purchases took place in Tournament Hills, an upscale community in Summerlin, shortly after the UFC was sold for $4 billion. Property records reported by the Las Vegas Review-Journal showed that White acquired homes measuring about 7,700, 5,500 and 4,700 square feet. Demolition permits were also issued for four homes in the area, including White’s existing residence, although the full extent of the planned work was unclear at the time.How did Dana White spend $6.2 million buying three neighboring mansions in Summerlin?Dana White’s property purchases began in October 2016 and continued into the following year. The three houses stood close to his existing home in Tournament Hills, a gated residential community in Summerlin, Las Vegas.According to the Las Vegas Review-Journal, which reported the purchases using property records, the first house measured about 7,700 square feet and cost just under $1.8 million. White then bought a 5,500-square-foot property for $2.4 million in January 2017. In March, he purchased a third house measuring nearly 4,700 square feet for $2 million.Together, the three purchases came to approximately $6.2 million. Their locations also mattered. Rather than buying houses spread across Las Vegas, White chose properties close to his existing residence, giving him control over a much larger stretch of the neighbourhood.His original home in Tournament Hills had been purchased in 2006. The Las Vegas Review-Journal reported that he paid $1.95 million for it from Frank Fertitta III, who had previously co-owned the UFC with his brother Lorenzo Fertitta.The timing of the later purchases was notable. In July 2016, the Fertitta brothers sold the UFC to a group led by WME-IMG in a deal reported to be worth $4 billion. White had been part of the organisation’s leadership for years and held an ownership stake.The property purchases followed that major business deal, but there is no publicly confirmed breakdown showing how much of White’s personal proceeds from the sale went towards the houses.Why did Dana White seek demolition permits for the Las Vegas properties?Buying three expensive houses next to one another was only part of the story. Records cited by the Las Vegas Review-Journal showed that demolition permits had been issued for four homes in Tournament Hills from November 2016 onwards.One house had been demolished by May 2017, according to a local real estate agent quoted in the report. The four properties included White’s existing residence, but the report said the full scope of the construction work was unclear at the time.The permits pointed to plans for major changes to the properties. However, they did not establish that all four houses were demolished immediately or confirm every detail of the final development.The purchases and demolition work created the possibility of joining neighbouring plots into a larger private estate. This would give White more space to shape the grounds around his home rather than keeping the existing houses and their separate layouts.There is also an important distinction between the documented purchases and later descriptions of the property. The $6.2 million figure relates to the three houses bought between October 2016 and March 2017. It does not represent the total cost of buying the original home, demolishing buildings, landscaping the grounds or carrying out later construction.Similarly, there is no confirmed public accounting of the complete development costs. Claims that White spent a particular amount building a new compound should therefore be treated separately from the documented purchase prices.What facilities can be seen inside Dana White’s Las Vegas mansion?White has given viewers a look inside his Las Vegas home, revealing several features linked to his interests outside the UFC.In April 2020, he appeared in a home tour for Haute TV, showing how he spent his time during the coronavirus lockdown. The footage offered a look at the property’s swimming pool, basketball court, gym and gaming area.The sports facilities are among the most recognisable parts of the house. White is a longtime Boston Celtics supporter, and his basketball court features the team’s logo. He has also shown himself practising his shots on the court.The home has a gaming area filled with arcade machines, including racing and fighting games. The setup gives White another way to spend his free time without leaving the property. A swimming pool and outdoor seating areas also feature in the home tour.Brazilian sports website ge.globo.com reported on White’s lockdown activities on May 3, 2020, describing the basketball court, arcade games, gym and pool shown in the footage. The report also noted that his home had a grass volleyball court and a collection of board games.These details are supported by the footage and published accounts of the property. However, claims about the exact number of interconnected pools, private chef facilities, cold-plunge units and other specialised amenities need separate confirmation. They should not be presented as established facts simply because they appear in descriptions of luxury homes.The same caution applies to the reported $50 million valuation. Sports Illustrated’s Athlete Lifestyle section described White’s Las Vegas residence as being worth $50 million in an October 2024 article. That figure is a reported estimate, not a confirmed sale price or an official valuation of the combined property.The available reports establish that White owns a large Las Vegas residence with several leisure and sports facilities. They do not provide a full, independently verified breakdown of the home’s current market value or the total cost of its development.How does Dana White’s Las Vegas home fit into his wider property holdings?The Summerlin residence is not the only Las Vegas property associated with White. He previously owned another large home connected to The Ultimate Fighter, the reality show that helped introduce UFC fighters to a wider audience.According to reports about the property, White listed that mansion for $5 million in 2019. The house measured about 9,500 square feet and had been used during the filming of the show. The asking price, however, should not be confused with a confirmed final sale price without supporting transaction records.White also has a connection to Maine, where he spent part of his childhood. His property interests there have received attention in recent years, including reports about his purchase of homes connected to his family history.His Las Vegas residence remains closely linked to his work in mixed martial arts. As UFC CEO and president, White has played a major role in the organisation’s growth since the early 2000s. The UFC’s 2016 sale marked a major change in the company’s ownership and brought significant attention to the finances of its leading figures.The story of White’s Summerlin property is best understood through the facts that are available: three neighbouring homes purchased for about $6.2 million, demolition permits issued for four properties, and a large residence with facilities he has shown publicly.The reported $50 million valuation gives an idea of how the estate has been described in later coverage, but the exact cost of construction and the current value of the combined property have not been established through a public accounting.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Maria Sharapova bought a Manhattan Beach lot for $4.1 million and built a three-story Japanese-inspired mansion; after 13 years, it sold for a record $25 million
articles.summary: Maria Sharapova turned a $4.1 million land purchase into a $25 million property sale in Manhattan Beach, California.
articles.body: Maria Sharapova turned a $4.1 million land purchase into a $25 million property sale in Manhattan Beach, California. The five-time Grand Slam champion bought the ocean-view lot in 2012, worked with architects to build a custom three-story home, and sold it to NBA star Luka Dončić in 2025. The deal set a residential sale record for Manhattan Beach. The house features Japanese-inspired design, concrete walls, large glass doors, a swimming pool and a two-lane bowling alley. Sharapova built the property to suit her own taste before selling it after more than a decade.How did Maria Sharapova turn a $4.1 million Manhattan Beach lot into a luxury mansion?Sharapova bought the ocean-view land on 8th Street in Manhattan Beach in 2012, the same year she won the French Open and completed her career Grand Slam. The achievement made her one of the few players to win all four major tennis titles during her career.Instead of purchasing an existing house, Sharapova chose to build one from scratch. She worked with Los Angeles architecture firm KAA Design, led by architect Grant Kirkpatrick, to create a home that reflected her taste. Construction took about three years, and the house was completed in 2015.The property sits in Manhattan Beach’s Hill Section, an elevated neighbourhood known for its coastal views and large homes. Its location, around 20 miles southwest of downtown Los Angeles, offered Sharapova a private place to live while staying within reach of the city.According to Architectural Digest, Sharapova was closely involved in the design process. The house was also featured in the publication’s home tour series in 2019, giving readers a look at the space and its carefully chosen materials.The property became a long-term home for the retired tennis star before she decided to sell it in 2025. Its eventual $25 million sale showed how much buyers were willing to pay for a custom-built home in this part of Southern California.What makes Maria Sharapova’s Japanese-inspired Manhattan Beach mansion different?The three-story home was designed around Japanese influences, clean lines and a close connection between indoor and outdoor spaces. Rather than filling the house with ornate details, the design uses natural materials, large windows and open living areas.Concrete walls give the building a strong, simple look, while pale oak flooring and dark cedar add warmth. Black metal frames around the windows and glass doors bring the different materials together. Large glass panels also allow natural light into the living spaces and make it easier to move between the house and the outdoors.The house has five bedrooms and several spaces for relaxing or entertaining. Its outdoor area includes a swimming pool, a patio and seating areas. Greenery around parts of the property adds privacy without taking away from the modern design.One of the more unusual features sits below the main living areas: a two-lane bowling alley. It gives the home a private entertainment space that is different from the usual luxury-house features, such as a gym or cinema.There is also a notable feature missing from the property. Despite Sharapova’s long career as a professional tennis player, she did not build a tennis court on the grounds. The home was designed as a place to relax away from the demands of competition, rather than as an extension of her training life.The result was a house built around the owner’s preferences instead of a standard design intended to appeal to as many buyers as possible. That personal touch helped make the property stand out when it came time to sell.Why did Maria Sharapova sell her Manhattan Beach home in 2025?Sharapova retired from professional tennis in 2020 after a career that included five Grand Slam singles titles and a rise to world No. 1. She had also built business interests outside the sport, including her candy brand Sugarpova and other commercial ventures.Her family life changed during the years that followed. Sharapova became engaged to British businessman Alexander Gilkes in 2020, and the couple welcomed their son, Theodore, in 2022. Gilkes co-founded the auction company Paddle8 and later became involved in the business venture studio Squared Circles.The couple’s plans to spend more time in Europe were cited as a reason for selling the California home. Maintaining a large property can require time and money, particularly when its owners are spending more of the year elsewhere.Sharapova began offering the house for sale in July 2025, with an asking price of $24.995 million. The Wall Street Journal reported the planned sale and noted that the home had ocean views but no tennis court.The asking price was far above the typical cost of a home in Manhattan Beach. The property was not simply a large house near the coast; it had been designed for Sharapova and included features that would be difficult to find together in another home.Sharapova also owned other properties in California. In January 2024, she bought a five-bedroom estate in Montecito from philanthropist Ann Lurie for $11.5 million in an all-cash deal. She had also purchased a five-acre ranch in Summerland for $8.6 million in 2020, according to the Montecito Journal.Those purchases show that selling the Manhattan Beach home did not mean leaving California real estate behind. Instead, it formed part of a wider property portfolio.How did Luka Dončić’s $25 million purchase set a Manhattan Beach record?NBA star Luka Dončić bought Sharapova’s Manhattan Beach mansion for $25 million in an off-market deal that closed at the end of August 2025. The sale was reported publicly in September, making the property one of the most talked-about celebrity home transactions of the year.Dončić had recently signed a three-year, $165 million contract extension with the Los Angeles Lakers after joining the team earlier in 2025. Buying a home in Southern California gave the basketball star a property near his new team.According to Architectural Digest, the $25 million deal set a record for a residential sale in Manhattan Beach. It surpassed the previous high for a home in the coastal city, showing the price buyers may pay for a rare property with ocean views and a custom design.The sale also marked a major increase from the $4.1 million Sharapova paid for the land in 2012. The difference between the purchase price and the sale price is $20.9 million. However, that figure is a gross difference, not her final profit. It does not account for the cost of building the house, upkeep, taxes, selling expenses or other costs over the years.The deal’s full financial outcome for Sharapova has not been made public. Still, selling for $25 million after owning the property for around 13 years represents a substantial rise in the property’s reported value.For Dončić, the purchase brought a custom-built home with space for family life and entertaining. For Sharapova, it marked the end of a long-term project that began with buying an empty lot and turning it into a home shaped by her own ideas.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cucho Hernández, la primera baja que complica los planes de Néstor Lorenzo para el duelo con Chile
articles.standfirst: El delantero se lesionó del sóleo en el partido contra el Barcelona
articles.summary: El delantero se lesionó del sóleo en el partido contra el Barcelona
articles.body: Juan Camilo 'Cucho' Hernández se convirtió en la primera baja relevante en el radar de la Selección Colombia de cara a la fecha FIFA de noviembre. El delantero del Real Betis sufrió una lesión muscular en el sóleo proximal izquierdo durante el partido ante el Barcelona, y el plazo estimado de recuperación lo dejaría fuera de los dos amistosos ante Chile. La lesión llegó en un momento delicado para el atacante: venía de ser titular con el Betis, había iniciado la temporada con goles y asistencias, y buscaba recuperar un lugar en el proyecto de Néstor Lorenzo tras no ser convocado en la última ventana internacional. El incidente ocurrió el sábado 17 de octubre, en la derrota del Real Betis por 5-2 frente al FC Barcelona. Cucho Hernández arrancó como titular, pero fue reemplazado cerca del minuto 64 por Troy Parrott tras sentir molestias musculares. Este lunes 19 de octubre, el Betis confirmó el diagnóstico tras las pruebas médicas: un daño en la zona del sóleo proximal de la pierna izquierda. El club no precisó el grado de la lesión ni fijó una fecha exacta de regreso, y señaló que la reincorporación dependerá de su evolución. El sóleo es uno de los músculos de la pantorrilla, ubicado en la parte posterior de la pierna. Una lesión en esa zona suele afectar la capacidad de acelerar, frenar, saltar y sostener esfuerzos repetidos, aspectos esenciales para un delantero de área como Cucho. Por eso, aunque no sea una lesión de larga duración, exige un proceso de recuperación cuidadoso para evitar recaídas. El Real Betis evitó dar un plazo oficial, pero la prensa española estima que Cucho podría estar entre tres y seis semanas fuera de las canchas, con un pronóstico más repetido de alrededor de un mes. Ese escenario es el que golpea directamente sus opciones con Colombia. Los amistosos ante Chile están programados para el viernes 13 de noviembre, en el estadio Pascual Guerrero de Cali, y el martes 17 de noviembre, en el Estadio Nacional de Santiago. Si la baja se confirma en torno a un mes, Cucho apenas estaría comenzando o completando su rehabilitación cuando Lorenzo deba definir la lista. Incluso si alcanzara a recuperarse, llegaría sin ritmo competitivo, sin partidos oficiales recientes y con muy poco tiempo de trabajo con el grupo. Para Néstor Lorenzo, la lesión de Cucho no es una emergencia deportiva inmediata, pero sí una complicación de fondo. El delantero había sido parte del Mundial 2026 y, aunque no entró en la última convocatoria ante México, Paraguay y Perú, seguía siendo una opción concreta para el ataque. La Selección Colombia atraviesa una etapa de renovación. Lorenzo ha probado nombres nuevos y ha dejado por fuera a jugadores con experiencia internacional, entre ellos Johan Mojica, Yerry Mina y Santiago Arias, mientras mantiene un núcleo con futbolistas como Dávinson Sánchez, Richard Ríos, Jhon Lucumí y Gustavo Puerta. En ese contexto, Cucho necesitaba rendimiento y continuidad en el Betis para volver a discutir un lugar. La lesión le quita justamente eso: la posibilidad de llegar a noviembre con minutos, goles y una versión física óptima.

articles.title: Florida Gators get new bowl destination in SI's latest projections
articles.summary: Sports Illustrated projects Florida to face Wake Forest in the Gator Bowl following UF's upset win over Texas in Week 7.
articles.body:
Florida is heading to Jacksonville for a matchup with Wake Forest in the TaxSlayer Gator Bowl on Dec. 30, according to Sports Illustrated's latest postseason projections . The forecast comes days after UF went on the road to stun No. 7 Texas, snapping a two-game losing streak and restoring some momentum to Jon Sumrall's program.

The outlet previously pinned Florida against Penn State in the ReliaQuest Bowl in Tampa. While the Gators remain outside the playoff picture, they are reasonably within striking distance. Florida has now earned two wins over top-10 ranked opponents.

Though not the best-case scenario for Florida, Wake Forest would be a formidable foe after gaining national attention with a 6-1 start this season. The Demon Deacons climbed to No. 13 in ESPN's latest power rankings after downing California 41-7.

The Gators have a chance to add to their playoff resume with an Oct. 31 date with fourth-ranked Georgia in Atlanta after the bye week. Sumrall's team also travels to No. 12 Kentucky on Nov. 14. In the 12-team playoff era, Florida's postseason hopes are still realistic.

Many outlets' latest projections reflect a shakeup after Week 7, with Miami vaulting to the top of both the US LBM Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 . Florida landed at Nos. 24 and 20, respectively.

articles.title: Moggi: ‘Juventus lack a coach, the team didn’t play at all against Lazio’
articles.summary: Former Juventus general manager Luciano Moggi believes the Bianconeri lack a coach, insisting the team failed to turn up in Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Lazio...
articles.body:
Former Juventus general manager Luciano Moggi believes the Bianconeri lack a coach, insisting the team failed to turn up in Sunday's 3-0 home defeat to Lazio.

According to TMW , Moggi said in an interview: "I wouldn't say the team played badly yesterday. I'd say they didn't play at all. Talking about their performance is out of place, they didn't take to the field. If you listen to Bremer's comments, you understand the team's situation. The rest should be asked of those in charge, not me."

Lazio won at the Allianz Stadium through goals from Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru. Juve were jeered off and are now eight points behind leaders Inter and Lazio. Luciano Spalletti watched from the stands while serving a ban.

Captain Gleison Bremer criticised his teammates afterwards , saying he "can't carry everyone". Spalletti replied that the Brazilian was involved in the defeat as much as anyone.

TURIN, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Davide Frattesi of S.S. Lazio runs with the ball under pressure from Bremer of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SS Lazio at Allianz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images)

Moggi on Juventus performance: 'Bremer made a huge mistake'

"The coach is missing, that's the underlying problem," Moggi said. "If Bremer says that publicly, that's fair enough, but in my view he made a huge mistake on the third goal. He escorted the player for 500 metres and let him shoot. Everyone is only looking after their own patch."

Spalletti admitted after the game that he was no longer sure the squad were following him.

"Those are certainties he shouldn't have. Nothing is certain right now," Moggi said. "When you hear comments like these, injuries are no excuse."

VIGO, SPAIN – OCTOBER 15: Luciano Spalletti, Head Coach of Juventus, reacts during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

Asked whether Spalletti should be at risk, with supporters calling for Antonio Conte, he replied: "Ask the fans. I can't judge from the outside."

Moggi tipped Inter and Roma for the Scudetto, "more Inter than Roma, but both, because they're the most compact and best-run sides". He was also blunt on Massimiliano Allegri's struggling Napoli: "They set out to get results and they're not getting them. Right now, they no longer know how to win."

articles.title: What We Learned: Purdue Boilermakers
articles.summary: What we learned from a strange 38-26 win against Purdue!
articles.body:
Man, that was weird. On Friday night, the Huskies snapped a 3 game skid, beating Purdue 38-26, despite 5 turnovers. Let's get to what we learned!

Throughout most of this game, I marveled at the sheer insanity of what was taking place. That's about as "drunk" of a game as I've yet seen. From the opening interception, I was convinced that the Huskies were going to continue their slide. But, let's give credit where credit is due. Elijah Brown hung in there, and looked pretty good, in spite of the 3 interceptions. 302 yards and 3 touchdowns is not bad for a backup. And just going by qualitative results, when he was able to find his guys, he looked pretty comfortable, dishing the ball to his receivers so they could make plays out in space. That led to the Huskies going 4 of 7 on third down, by far their best effort of the season. But it wasn't all on Brown. The running game also looked the best it had all year. Down to what felt like their 8th or 9th running back (but in actuality, they were down to their 4th or 5th), it looked like it was going to be another uphill battle. Enter Trey Cooley.

A frequent target of my derision, Cooley had never tallied more than 22 yards all season, coming into West Lafayette averaging about 2 yards per carry. He had double that (and then some) on one 53 yard touchdown run in the 4th quarter. When the clock hit 0, Cooley had 113 yards on 8 carries, along with Brian Bonner's 13 for 64 and another touchdown. It was the most complete rushing performance the Huskies have had to this point in the season. Which is ironic, considering where the depth is in the running back room. Even Dezmen Roebuck and Chris Lawson got in the backfield for a few carries! It all comes down to adjusting what you call based on what personnel you have, and Coach Fisch made sure to highlight that in his postgame presser. "… the best opportunity we can give you to put you guys in the best possible position. And then as players, we need you guys to tell us what you want, to tell us what you need, to tell us what types of runs are best for you… I think Coach (Michael) Switz(er) did an amazing job this week of really listening to what those guys felt good about, and I think they put together a really good running plan." If this kind of coaching continues, then maybe this offense can be a part of salvaging the season?

The defense, while continuing to give up the big play, held Fame Ijeboi to 19 yards on 13 carries, after he torched the Golden Gophers last week for 195 yards and 3 touchdowns. While giving up 273 passing yards is not ideal (and to that point, neither is giving up 116 receiving yards to one receiver), that's a major feather in this defense's collective cap, especially after a disastrous performance last week against Iowa. But even then, this defense forced 2 interceptions, so that's also something to build on. Alex McLaughlin continued to do what he's always done, flying to the ball and being in on so many tackles, finishing with a team leading 7. The defense also stood firm when they absolutely had to, holding Purdue to 5/14 on 3rd down and 1/4 on fourth down. They also sacked Ryan Browne 3 times, all the while holding him to a 51% completion percentage, which is a pretty good mark, considering his efficiency coming into this game stood at about 69%. It was an absolutely needed performance to right the ship, and this unit played really hard in order to do that. Going into the bye week is yet another opportunity to get right ahead of a tilt with a Nebraska squad sitting at 5-1. Still, there's a nagging fear that this performance may have been fool's gold, considering the inconsistent play from a unit that was hyped as one of the best in the Big Ten in the preseason. It all comes down to 2 things: how good Purdue's offense ends up being and if the Huskies' defense can maintain positive momentum against Nebraska and beyond.

So, after this performance, I had one overarching question. Is this team good, or bad? It's a common question, given what we've seen in the past few weeks. There are certainly signs of a good football team in here if you know where to look. The running game got going, the top receivers had 103 and 97 yards (Chris Lawson and Dezmen Roebuck respectively), and the defense got 2 interceptions, so we're good, right?

Not so fast my friend! Elijah Brown still had 3 interceptions in spite of his 302 yards and 3 touchdowns, and some of his passes definitely looked shaky coming out. We're still banged up at running back, and I don't know if the defense is any good, considering that big plays and penalties are still an overarching issue for Fisch in year 3. But the playcalling for a backup quarterback was solid, and when Brown got in rhythm, he was finding his receivers with regularity. While those words from Fisch were encouraging, only time will tell whether he keeps this approach, though I believe he should. Calling what your players are comfortable with can only be a good thing, right? And it's great to see the emergence of Bonner and Cooley, even as they are banged up right now.

Time will tell whether the team will look different coming off the bye. There's a chance that Demond starts at Nebraska, but there's also a chance that Brown gets the ball again. If you're Coach Fisch, I honestly think you need to give Brown more reps, seeing as how the team seemed to respond to Brown more than Williams. Chris Lawson was also hobbled a bit, as he jogged off on the same play as Brian Bonner (Lawson's knee was bandaged, but he appeared unconcerned post game), so we'll see if the bye helps him recover. We also have to take a look at the ancillary running backs as well, like Ansu Sanoe (who was battling the flu bug) to see if they're available.

The ultimate question from this game is this: does this game define the 2026 Huskies as good or bad? Well, your guess, dear reader, is as good as mine. Because I don't know. One game doesn't typically define a season, good or bad. But I left feeling very encouraged about some things, and that's better than I would've said a week ago. Let's hope the coaches and players use the week off to help get right, and we'll see if this performance is a sign of improvement or just a mirage!

There's a much needed bye next week, before the Dawgs make their journey to Lincoln to play Nebraska on Halloween! Go Dawgs!

articles.title: Colts get brutal reality check with Daniel Jones as 'biggest mistake' of offseason
articles.summary: This is unfortunately a justified label for Daniel Jones and the Colts.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are currently 2-4 this year, following a loss to the Tennessee Titans . After such a brutal loss, the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard.

There are plenty of things he's done wrong over the years, but recently Ballard's moves have not gone well at all. The Sauce Gardner trade was a huge mistake, and the Alec Pierce extension hasn't gone well. But the worst might be the Daniel Jones deal.

ESPN's Dan Graziano blasted the Colts over the Jones contract extension, as he believes that the notion that Jones' extension was the "biggest mistake" made by any team this offseason is not an overreaction.

Daniel Jones extension called 'biggest mistake' of offseason

"The Daniel Jones extension was the biggest mistake any team made this offseason," Graziano writes. "Verdict: Not an overreaction."

Graziano didn't stop there; he also asked a brutal question that the Colts have to come to terms with: "Could it get better? Sure. Lots of things can happen. But how much better can we really expect things to get in Indy?"

This is a brutal reality check of the Jones contract for the Colts. While there might be hope that he can somewhat turn things around, even if he does, it most likely won't result in a deep playoff run.

There are plenty of other issues on this roster, and even if Jones does turn into the quarterback he showed he could be in the first half of 2025, this season might already be over for the Colts.

Ballard has been fired, the Colts don't have their 2027 first-round pick, the team is 2-4, and they just lost to the Titans. Jones is making close to $50 million guaranteed on a two-year, $88 million deal.

This contract for Jones hasn't worked out as the Colts had hoped, and Graziano is calling it the biggest mistake made by any team this offseason.

While some other moves are looking like blunders in retrospect around the league, this contract from the Colts for Jones is one of the worst.

There's just not enough upside with Jones, and it seems more likely than not that Graziano is right in his brutal assessment of the Colts and their extension with Jones this past offseason.

articles.title: SEC's crazy, history-making Week 7 weekend is the latest example of college football's new era
articles.summary: Five AP Top-20 SEC teams lost in the same week for the first time this century, and the data shows why college football upsets keep surging.
articles.body: Week seven of the college football season was everything fans love about the sport. Chaos. Rivalries, like Tennessee-Alabama and Auburn-Georgia. Upsets, with BYU taking down Notre Dame in front of an exuberant home crowd in Provo. And debate over what it all means for the rest of the year. Not one team ranked in the AP Top 25 poll in week six stayed in the same position in the week seven poll. Texas dropped 12 spots. Florida gained 12. Multiple other schools moved up or down at least six positions, with Missouri falling a whopping nine places after their blowout loss to Ole Miss. But no stat better exemplifies the chaos of week seven better than this one. Tom Fornelli from CBS Sports posted on X this week that, "The SEC is the first conference this century to have 5 AP Top-20 teams lose in the same week." WEEK 7 AP TOP 25 POLL FEATURES A COMPLETE SHUFFLE AFTER CHAOTIC WEEKEND, WITH MIAMI TAKING OVER THE TOP SPOT We're just a few months away from completing our 26th year in this century, somehow, and the SEC was the first conference in that time frame to have five teams rankedin the top-20 lose in just one weekend. That's pretty remarkable. And it's also a sign of things to come. We've known for some time that the advent of NIL and the transfer portal would change college football. But it doesn't seem like we've come fully to grips with just how quickly that change would happen and how much of an impact it would have on the sport. The reasons for this, and the results from it, are obvious. In decades past, a say, four-star recruit might choose to commit to Nick Saban's Alabama, or Pete Carroll's USC, hoping to play for championships and reach the NFL. Then find themselves losing out on a starting role to an even more highly regarded five-star player. With little recourse, short of transferring to sit out an entire season, that player likely would stay put, wait their turn, and hope they get their chance on the field. Now though, many of those players don't pick Georgia, Alabama, or USC in the first place. NIL has allowed smaller programs to compete for recruits they'd previously have missed out on. They might not offer the same coaching or championship aspirations, but they can offer something more immediately valuable: money. It's the same with the transfer portal. Lose out on a starting job? Hit the portal, go start elsewhere. Suddenly that four-star backup for Alabama is now a starter at Auburn or Tennessee. Again, it's obvious, but this weekend's chaos shows the result of this new era in practice: the gaps between teams are smaller than they've ever been. And we have the data to prove it. ESPN's SP+ ranking system is an efficiency-driven rating that measures success on offense, defense, and special teams, adjusted for tempo and opposition. Essentially, trying to use the most sustainable and predictive parts of a team's resume to remove some of the randomness inherent in sports. These ratings generally track very closely to those used by sports books to set their lines. And sports books are the best in the business at ranking the best teams, because their livelihood depends on it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Thus far in 2026, just a little over halfway through the season, there's a clear pattern: there's not nearly as much of a gap separating the top handful of teams from the back end of the top 25. And it's why we're seeing so many more upsets, with more likely coming the rest of the year. Ohio State is currently the number one team in the rating at 26.8, roughly corresponding to 27 points better than the median college football team, around the 70th best in the country, for example. Georgia is right behind at 26.5, then Miami at 25.3, Notre Dame at 24.8, and Indiana at 23.6. That's already very tightly bunched, but expanding it shows how close the margins are in college football this year. Utah, the No. 10 team in SP+, is rated at 19.4, just a touchdown behind OSU. Ole Miss, at No. 14, is 17.1, meaning they're less than a touchdown worse than Indiana. You can look all the way down to Kansas State at No. 25 and they're essentially one score worse than No. 9 BYU. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! So how does this compare to the pre-portal era? Well, looking back at 2022, it's apparent how much, and how quickly, things have changed. The 2022 Georgia Bulldogs, in the post-bowl results, had a 37.3 rating. They were over 37 points better than the median team, compared to Ohio State's 26.8 points in 2026. Georgia's 37 rating was a whopping 23 points better than the No. 25 team in that year's rankings, Arkansas. Halfway through the 2026 season, the gap between No. 1 and No. 25 is just 13 points. Georgia was 18 points better than the No. 10 team, funnily enough also Utah, in 2022. Right now, the gap between OSU and Utah is seven points. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Those are gigantic differences, and it's why the era of runaway dominance and multi-year dynasties seems to be at an end. Indiana's 2025 season was remarkable; running through an entire year undefeated in the portal, superconference, expanded playoff era is an incredible achievement. Even Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said prior to the season that he believed those days were over in college football. Then Indiana went 16-0. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD But already, in just week seven, there is only one undefeated team remaining in the Big Ten and SEC, combined. And it's UCLA. Just as everyone expected. Alabama has two losses. Georgia lost at home. Texas has two losses and is lucky not to have a third. Indiana's winning streak was snapped. Oregon has two losses and remains unranked. LSU spent about $150 million to hire Lane Kiffin and revamp their roster, and lost twice in the first six games. The gaps between teams is small, and shrinking. Which is why there are more upsets and surprises than even the typically chaotic college football season usually provides. Oh, and Ohio State just lost their starting quarterback for "several weeks," ahead of games against USC and Oregon. And in a perfect example of how this new era works, instead of another experienced, highly-ranked recruit backing Julian Sayin up, they're turning to a three-star true freshman to replace him. That hypothetical backup? He's probably starting somewhere else.

articles.title: Alba Petisco se mete con brillantez en la final del concurso completo del Mundial
articles.standfirst: El equipo femenino acaba en el puesto decimotercero con la subcampeona de Europa en 2025 como punta de lanza en un notable undécimo lugar
articles.summary: El equipo femenino acaba en el puesto decimotercero con la subcampeona de Europa en 2025 como punta de lanza en un notable undécimo lugar
articles.body: Alba Petisco salvó hoy la honrilla de la gimnasia artística española en el Mundial de Rotterdam (Países Bajos). La villarinense (aunque nacida en Cataluña) acabó undécima en la calificación y estará el próximo viernes en la final del concurso completo -junto a otras 23 gimnastas-, en la que buscará mejorar la decimocuarta plaza del pasado año en Yakarta (Indonesia). Laia Font concluyó en el puesto 35 y Aitana Pacheco, en el 48. La española, subcampeona de Europa hace un año en Leipzig y quinta este 2026 en Zagreb, volvió a dar la cara por un joven y prometedor equipo, el femenino (Alba Petisco, Laia Font, Aitana Pacheco, Marina Escudero, Laura Casabuena y Carlota Armenta), que terminó decimotercero con 155.963 puntos y sin ninguna representante en las finales por aparatos. Petisco es por tanto el único gimnasta español que sigue en competición pues el equipo masculino se fue de vacío el domingo tras acabar decimosexto y sin finalistas individuales. Cabe recordar que los ochos equipos en cada género que disputarán las dos finales colectivas se jugarán los tres primeros billetes por sexo para los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028. La española, de 23 años, sumó 53.599 puntos tras una actuación muy sólida –13.566 en la barra de equilibrio, 13.500 en las barras asimétricas, 13.300 en salto y 13.233 en suelo–. No se metió en finales por aparatos pero es tercera reserva en suelo. La calificación estuvo dominada por las chinas con 164.996 puntos, con las estadounidenses (164.529) y las rusas (163.662) segundas y terceras. Estas últimas aguantaron el tipo pese a la ausencia de la campeona mundial y europea, Angelina Melnikova, y sus compañeras Anna Kalmymoka y Viktoria Listunova, a las que Países Bajos denegó el visado de entrada. En el plano individual, la mejor fue la argelina criada en Francia Kaylia Nemour con 55.999 puntos, seguida de la estadounidense Skye Blakely (55.465) y la rusa Liudmila Roshchina (55.098). La china Qinqin Ke, de tan sólo 16 años y vigente campeona asiática, cometió más errores de los previstos en la clasificación y concluyó quinta con 54,699, pero en la final es clara candidata a los metales.

articles.title: Rams' tough start to 2026 season gets worse with Davante Adams injury update
articles.summary: Two games under.500 already, the Rams will be without their veteran star receiver moving forward.
articles.body:
So far this season, the Rams haven't been nearly the team many expected.

Entering 2026, L.A. was one of the Super Bowl favorites thanks to its star-studded roster, adding Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and Trent McDuffie to an elite offensive core. Flash forward to Monday, and the Rams sat at 2-4, coming off an ugly loss to the Cardinals with mounting injury concerns.

On top of absences for Garrett, McDuffie, tight end Terrance Ferguson and new kicker Blake Grupe, Sean McVay announced a longer-term absence for star receiver Davante Adams.

Here's how long Adams will be out and how it impacts the Rams' offense moving forward.

McVay said Monday that Adams will miss 6-to-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring, per Adam Schefter.

Adams left Sunday's game against the Cardinals with a non-contact injury in the final minutes, coming up limping after sprinting on a route:

Adams' timeline puts him on track to miss the Rams' season through at least November, if not all of December as well. The tail end of his 10-week timeline would be a return in Week 16 for a Christmas Day matchup with the Seahawks .

The Rams' injury issues didn't end with Adams on Monday — McVay also announced lengthy absences for defensive tackle Kobie Turner and Grupe:

Puka Nacua has remained the focal point of the Rams' high-powered passing attack, which has helped lead the offense to a No. 3-ranking 401.3 yards per game. Nacua, however, won't be able to take much of a wider workload, targeted 52 times over four games this season.

In Adams' absence, it's likely the Rams look for Mumpfield (8 catches, 127 yards, TD) and Whittington (2 catches, 12 yards) to step up in the receiver room, while Matthew Stafford will also likely be looking at his tight ends more often.

Tyler Higbee has become a reliable weapon for Stafford lately, posting 24 catches for 246 yards and a touchdown so far.

Adams' work in the red zone will be the toughest aspect to replace, scoring 14 touchdowns in 2025 and four so far in 2026.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts’ apparent season-ending injury leaves Eagles with tough questions about blood clots in his lungs
articles.summary: At just 28 years old, and only 20 months removed from being named the Super Bowl MVP, Jalen Hurts is now on blood thinners to stave off what – without them – could be life-threatening blood clots in his lungs.
articles.body: At just 28 years old, and only 20 months removed from being named the Super Bowl MVP, Jalen Hurts is now on blood thinners to stave off what – without them – could be life-threatening blood clots in his lungs. The Associated Press and others are reporting that the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback won’t play again this season, which would appear an obvious outcome since treatment for Hurts’ injuries – bilateral pulmonary emboli and deep vein thrombosis in medical jargon – requires three months on the blood thinners. That much everyone can agree on. It is everything in between that makes the situation less cut-and-dry. The Eagles, in conjunction with Hurts’ agent Nicole Lynn, have released two statements in the past four days detailing Hurts’ injury and treatment, citing the “interest of transparency.” The timeline breaks down like this: Left unanswered are two critical issues. For starters, why was Hurts permitted to fly across the Atlantic twice? Along with injury, as in Hurts’ case, deep vein thrombosis can be caused by extended periods sitting on long flights, pulmonary critical care expert Dr. Parth Rali told CNN. The International Air Transport Association guidelines stipulate that “travelers with a recent DVT of the legs may fly once they are asymptomatic and stable on anticoagulants.” A bigger question, though, is why was Hurts permitted to play in the game at all? At best, he was coming off a handful of hours of rest after a stressful night in the hospital. At worst, he was competing with a serious medical condition. During his normally scheduled Monday news conference, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni did not go into detail about either decision, only repeatedly saying that he trusted his medical team and that “it’s not just me that cares deeply about our players, it’s them as well.” Sirianni added that this was the same medical team that “helped 21 of 22 guys be available for the Super Bowl.” Asked how Hurts was feeling, the coach said he would keep his private conversations private. “But I haven’t been without him for an extended period of time,” Sirianni said. “I miss him.” As Sirianni spoke on a live-streamed interview, the chat box down the right side of the video erupted with unanswered questions. Even before the announcement about Hurts, Sirianni and the Eagles were on a short leash with their notoriously hard-to-please fan base. Philadelphia has lost four games in a row, the team’s worst skid in Sirianni’s six seasons. Along with the usual “fire Sirianni” suggestions, fans directed their ire at Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie and general manager Howie Roseman, who did not make themselves available for comment. Some called them cowards; others opted for more colorful language. Most, however, questioned whether Hurts’ safety had been sacrificed in the name of the sport. “Super Bowl MVP has been done wrong,” one wrote. Added another, “Players’ health is at the forefront of our mind? Obviously not.” Still another simply called the decision “shameful” and wondered who “put his life at risk.” Deep vein thromboses, while rare, are not entirely uncommon among athletes. In February 2020, San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama was diagnosed with one in his shoulder, undergoing immediate surgery to prevent it from spreading to his lungs. Brandon Ingram was shut down with a DVT in his shoulder in 2019 and Serena Williams was hospitalized with multiple pulmonary embolisms in her lungs, the result of a blood clot forming after she cut her foot.

articles.title: Anaheim Ducks Prepare Multiple Lineup Changes For Rangers Clash
articles.summary: The Anaheim Ducks return to the ice on Monday night, looking to rebound as they square off against the New York Rangers.Ville Husso will get the nod to man t...
articles.body:
The Anaheim Ducks return to the ice on Monday night, looking to rebound as they square off against the New York Rangers.

Ville Husso will get the nod to man the Ducks' net, as reported by Stephen Whyno and Daily Faceoff. Husso has seen action in two games this season, with one start. He's 1-0-0 and is currently rocking a .935 save percentage and a 1.58 GAA.

In his lone start in 2026-27, Husso made 27 saves on 29 shots against the Calgary Flames. Husso, however, will face a greater challenge on Monday. The Flames were struggling to put goals up when he faced them, but the Rangers are a bit of a different story.

New York is 11th in goals scored with 28 through 10 games. That said, they are coming off a shutout loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets, and have scored just once in their previous two contests.

It was the second time an opponent shut out the Rangers this season, with the first coming in their season opener to the Boston Bruins . New York rebounded following that matchup, defeating the Tampa Bay Lightning 5-1.

Offensively, the Ducks will face Dylan Garand, as Daily Faceoff and Vincent Mercogliano have confirmed. Garand has played well filling in for the injured Igor Shesterkin, posting a 3-2-1 record, a .927 save percentage, a 1.81 GAA, and a shutout. He could give the Ducks' scorers a challenge.

Anaheim Ducks Projected Lines And Pairings Against Rangers

Daily Faceoff and Zach Cavanagh have Alex Killorn, Leo Carlsson, and Nikita Klepov taking the first line. Carlsson continues to pace the Ducks in scoring with nine points and two goals through seven matchups.

Mikael Granlund appears to be returning after missing the previous matchup vs. Boston. Before going down with an injury, Granlund was on a tear , scoring at least one point in his first six matchups. He is slated to man the second line with Frank Vatrano and Beckett Sennecke at the wings.

Roger McQueen is slated as the third-line center, with A.J. Greer and Cutter Gauthier taking the wings. Gauthier played the previous game at center in Granlund's absence, but struggled to win draws . And finally, Tim Washe looks to center Jeff Malott and Judd Caulfield. Washe has been rather productive, with four points and two goals in seven games.

As for the defensive pairings, Jackson LaCombe is projected to line up alongside Noah Warren. LaCombe continues to put together a solid campaign early on, with six points and a goal in seven games. Tyson Hinds and Tristan Luneau look like the middle pair, while Pavel Mintyukov and Nick Jensen are the projected third pair.

Drew Helleson, Sam Colangelo, and Nikita Nesterenko are projected to be scratched. Troy Terry and Ryan Poehling remain out, as is Ian Moore.

Ducks And Rangers Facing Higher-Than-Normal Stakes Early

Both teams are raring to get a win after losing their previous contests. Anaheim is currently in fifth place in the Pacific this season with eight points and is hoping they won't fall behind what looks like a tough division. They are already eight points behind the division-leading Vegas Golden Knights .

The Rangers find themselves in the opposite situation. They are second in the Metropolitan Division behind the Carolina Hurricanes . For New York, it's all about keeping up with Carolina, who currently have 15 points compared to the Rangers' 13.

This is one of those early-season matchups where one team can't afford to fall much further behind its division leader. As for the other, it's all about matching them. The puck drops at 7:00 p.m. EDT.

articles.title: Sixers discuss key points when it comes to defeating Knicks in opener
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers discuss the key points when it comes to defeating the New York Knicks in the opener.
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- The Philadelphia 76ers will look to make a statement on opening night when they take on the defending champion New York Knicks on Tuesday night. The Sixers will look to make things happen at Madison Square Garden and spoil ring night for the champs.

The last time these two teams met was in the playoffs when the Knicks swept the Sixers out of Round 2 back in May. Now? Philadelphia is a much different-looking team with the additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown along with some additions to the bench unit. The Sixers are in a great position to dethrone the Knicks in the coming season.

With that being said, the Knicks are a team that knows who they are. They play hard, have great chemistry, and they attack the glass led by Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, and others. Keeping them off the glass could be the difference in a close game.

"I think it's obviously one of their major strengths, right?" said coach Nick Nurse. "Like it's at the top of the list of what needs to go well. Like, they cannot just be collecting a ton of offensive rebounds, kicking them out and hitting 3s. It's Hart. It's OG. It's Bridges. It's Deuce (McBride). It's (Jordan) Clarkson. So, they've done a good job. I think the role guys have excelled, and I've probably forgot one or two guys too in there. But still, that's a major strength of theirs to win those extra possessions, and that makes a difference in a close game."

Hart, Anunoby, and Bridges are three perimeter players who crash the boards and rebound with reckless abandon. They are three players the Sixers are certainly going to have to figure out as they head into this matchup as they have given Philadelphia trouble in the past.

Nurse and the staff will also have to figure out what to do with Towns. Will the Sixers put Joel Embiid on Towns? Or have James or Brown defend him and have Embiid be something of a roamer. There are different ways for Philadelphia to defend the New York star if the Sixers go with a 4 on him instead of the traditional center.

"It allows you to switch a little more on the screen-and-rolls, right?" Nurse acknowledged. "That's a big one. Allows you maybe to get back to the pick-and-pop game a little bit, or take it out. You can play maybe a couple more coverages with that. I mean, the cons are: is can Towns pass over the 4? Can he rebound over the 4? Can he post up over the 4? Can he shoot over the 4?"

The Knicks will certainly be a tough challenge for the Sixers as they feature a strong roster that is coming off winning a championship and they have a ton of cohesion. Philadelphia doesn't have that quite yet. Therefore, Nurse is looking for the fight and the competitive level from his team.

"Just making tough plays," he stated. "Are we gonna fight through screens? Are we gonna put our body on people? Are we gonna rebound? Are we gonna set physical screens? Are we gonna protect the rim? You know, those kind of things. I think the physicality and the small big things."

Tip off in the season opener is set for 7 p.m. EDT on Tuesday.

articles.body:
ROTTERDAM, Netherlands — The U.S. women are going to be busy the rest of this week.

In addition to competing in the team final Wednesday, Oct. 21, Claire Pease, Skye Blakely and Reese Esponda all qualified for individual event finals.

The top 24 gymnasts, with a limit of two per country, make the all-around final. The top eight on each event, again with a limit of two per country, make the apparatus final.

US women shine at gymnastics world championships in Netherlands

What world championship finals did USA Gymnastics make?

Blakely will be in four finals. Despite the Americans being in the very first qualifying session, and judging getting more generous in the latter rounds, Blakely finished with the second-highest all-around score. She also made the finals on vault (fifth), uneven bars (eighth) and balance beam (sixth).

Pease also will be in the all-around final, finishing seventh overall in qualifying. She'll also be in the vault (third) and floor (fifth) finals.

Esponda held her spot atop the floor standings, with no one else getting within 0.20 points of her. Impressive, considering Esponda had to change her routine after learning right before worlds began that she wasn't going to get credit for one of her skills.

"I was a little bit upset about it just because that was a big connection pass for me," Esponda said. "I move forward. It is what it is."

The women's all-around final is Friday, Oct. 23. The vault and uneven bars finals are Saturday, Oct. 24, and the balance beam and floor exercise finals are Sunday, Oct. 25.

articles.title: Commanders Get Major News on WR Stefon Diggs Before 49ers Game
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders have an opportunity to rebound in a big way after last week’s depleted tie against the New York Giants.On Monday night, the Command...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have an opportunity to rebound in a big way after last week's depleted tie against the New York Giants.

On Monday night, the Commanders will take on the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on the road at Levi's Stadium.

Ahead of the matchup, Washington had several question marks regarding the status of players across the roster. One was veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who missed last week's game with a hamstring injury.

Hours before kickoff, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Diggs, after practicing for several days this week, is trending toward playing against San Francisco.

Barring an unforeseen setback before the game, Diggs will rejoin the offense, giving quarterback Jayden Daniels a much-needed boost by returning one of his top and most reliable weapons.

Via Schefter: "Stefon Diggs also trending towards playing tonight."

Diggs won't be the only player returning to the Commanders' lineup Monday night.

Schefter also reported that cornerback Trey Amos will make his season debut after coming off injured reserve. Washington will also get back linebacker Jordan Magee and running back Jeremy McNichols .

McNichols' return could be significant because starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has been placed on injured reserve alongside outside linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste .

In some other notable corresponding moves, the Commanders announced before kickoff that they released linebacker Austin Keys and elevated outside linebacker T.J. Maguranyanga for Monday night's game.

Washington enters the matchup at 1-3-1. If they lose, the NFC East would make NFL history as the first division to go winless for two consecutive weeks.

articles.title: Q&A Recap: Jared Benko’s introductory press conference
articles.summary: Jared Benko spoke to the media Monday morning at the Sukup End Zone Club. Benko, a University of Georgia alumnus, will be the 15th athletic director in Iowa...
articles.body:
Jared Benko spoke to the media Monday morning at the Sukup End Zone Club. Benko, a University of Georgia alumnus, will be the 15th athletic director in Iowa State history. He officially starts on Oct. 30, pending approval from the Iowa Board of Regents.

The following is a question " Q: " and answer "Benko:" transcript.

Q: You told us in the opening statement why Iowa State. To zoom out a bit, I want to ask why a place like Iowa State here in the Big 12, where, and pardon me for using a strawman argument, some may say teams in the Big 12 have hit their ceiling, a lot of them, it might not get the same level of resources as some brand names like your previous employer, Auburn, or your alma mater, Georgia or other teams in the SEC and the Big 10. Why is it that this type of school and specifically this school appealed to you?

Benko: I wouldn't be here if I thought Iowa State had hit its ceiling. In today's world, there's the economics of college athletics. Everyone has their headwinds and challenges. I think, to me, what gives me great confidence here is you can't undervalue the fan base here. When I first got in the process and you look at since 2011, averaging over 50,000 fans in football, 12,000 in men's basketball and north of 6-8,000 in women's basketball, that's unbelievable. So, first and foremost, you've got the fan base here that supports day in, day out. You can't undervalue or overstate that enough. Two, I think it also is about people in alignment. I mean, with the job that Jamie did here and whatother staff have done from a, fiscal management standpoint, it really positioned Iowa State to do all these investments and facilities.

I would say that I still like the best is yet to come and really CyTown development, I think it's a really kind of a look-in of, of the innovation that can come. But listen, every school in the country is having to, to turn over every rock to find different revenue streams. The great thing here is there's been a long history of managing money well, but in today's world, you've got to also produce it. I think this is a tremendous foundation. I've spent time mostly in, in small college towns or rural areas, and this is a great fit for us as a family. It checked all the boxes.

Q: Your interesting background when you started Starkville, places before that, but then Georgia, Southern, Auburn, what makes you uniquely qualified in your opinion for this athletic department?

Benko: I think in today's world, you have to be fluent in every facet of a department. For a long time we all kind of came up through specialties, right? Mine was through finance and tremendous skill set to have. I think the time at Georgia Southern leading the department where I was mostly external raising resources and again where you had no backstop, had tremendous alignment and support, but no backstop. Even at Auburn, where you're competing against some of the largest resource schools in the country, you really focus a lot on revenue generation, but then you tackle on the front office management. That's been a change for all of us post-House settlement where you've got to build out a front office, you've got contracts, negotiations. Every core facet of responsibility that you need to really be successful, I feel like in this role, I feel like I've done at a high level with, with some, building out some really high-performing teams.

The reality is you're only as good as those around you, and we've got a great team at Iowa State, and it's not just me, it's gonna be everyone in the department pulling together. That was the mission or really the, the vision today to lead out to our department was saying, hey, listen, this is gonna take a, it's gonna take a village to get Iowa State to where we want o, get it to, but we have some incredible people here. So I think it's past experiences and I think it's a tremendous foundation that Jamie laid that really gives me confidence that we can take this place in new heights.

Q: Most of your résumé has a lot of SEC schools, but what were some things that you felt you could have only learned at Georgia Southern as your time as an AD there that helped enhance the way you approach your job when you returned to Auburn and now when you come here to Iowa State?

Benko: When you become an AD or any role in life, right, you don't really know what to expect until you get in the role, right? And so. I think we'd be remiss that there's things that you go back and say, man, I really did a great job there and I could have done better here. I do think when you, anytime you lead an organization, you find out, one, it just, it's sometimes more affirmation of how you want to lead, right? But also two, you realize when you're at a place at a group of six school, where again, we have tremendous support, tremendous alignment, but the resources aren't there. Sometimes you have to measure 3-4 times before you cut, and I think that, that really honed in on me of being resourceful.

So whether you're leading the department of 150 employees or leading one with over 500, there's a lot of similarities there. I left Georgia Southern because I saw the change in the landscape and really with post-House and so seeing where the front office piece and the contracts were going, I wanted to make sure I was at the tip of the spear. To work with the SEC office and others to make sure, cause listen, we're all drivers, like really hyper-competitive. I want to be one of the best in the country. Part of that was getting back to the SEC, taking what I learned at Georgia Southern, which a lot of the leadership skills, a lot of the external experience that you also need, and then you get a chance to really use it at Auburn, and the great thing we did at Auburn, again, we have a fantastic leadership from the president on down to the AD. We have the ability to cross-pollinate across departments, and that's not usual. A lot of times departments get saladed up and kind of have their, their various responsibilities. At Auburn, we've done a great job of cross-pollinating, working across the aisle, and I think all that is a culmination of the experience that I have.

Q: W hen it comes to the future, which of course is rife with uncertainty as you all have referenced, how does innovation play in when it comes to probably sometimes you need to take bold swings, sometimes you have to take a measured approach? It's a case by case basis, I'm sure as fast as it moves.

Benko: There's obviously, sometimes you come into an organization, there's low-hanging fruit, and there's sometimes, I think the CyTown piece is a great example of innovation that really runs through campus and runs through the leadership. We're not gonna be innovative just to be innovative, but I do think that what you're seeing is college sports for a long time has been a decade behind professional sports. When you look at the professional sports model, they've been owners and operators, an, they're commercial entities oftentimes are more profitabl, than the, the teams that they actually own and operate. So for us, With our fan base and again our donor base who's been so supportive, we're always gonna make sure that everything we do is to position our student-athletes for success on and off the field. You have to continue to find ways to improve the economic engine. So that commercialization piece is what we're gonna be looking at. Listen, we're gonna bring some different events and initiatives to Ames that may seem out of left field, and we're not afraid to fail at times and, and fail forward and try to learn from it.

But we're gonna be innovative in everything we do, and I think part of that is there's some things that I think will really be again, low-hanging fruit. There's some things we're gonna need to sit and marinate on and talk to people, but I'm not as concerned with that cause innovation runs through the heart of this campus, and we're hopefully and excited to be part of that.

Q: You've talked a lot about attacking change and turning over every rock for revenue. How have you done that and how will you do that here while still keeping the games and athletics affordable and accessible for fans and students?

Benko: I think that's, that's why you do it, right? I think part of it is there's some schools out there that are just tax the consumer, and I think one want to make sure you tell the fans thank you and the supporters and the donors and alumni, thank you, because this is not possible without them. I do think that what you're seeing are different ways to bring new offerings to fans. Oftentimes they go to an MLB ballpark, an NBA game or NFL game, they're seeing, and so part of that is just trying to continue to learn more about the fan.

I'll give you a great example. Historically, you know, a fan purchases a ticket and maybe you have a little bit of information. But what we've done in the past is start connecting, what are their concession purchases, what are their retail purchases, and you start building profiles of ways we can continue to enhance their experience. I think part of that is using the past fan surveys and trying to make sure that we're listening to fans and being attentive. I think also what I've found, honestly, the best feedback from is getting out and visiting fans and tailgates, greeting them at the gates. I've done that before and I always appreciate candor, and some people will sometimes tell you more than you want to hear. All kidding aside, you just gotta be humble enough to listen and learn and ultimately understand that we're gonna try some different things. So with Auburn, we've, I shared with President Cook a lot of things we've done. I's not just concerts, it's not just entertainment. We just had Nate Bargatze last week in comedy. So we're gonna continue to push the envelope, but hopefully, it's bringing things in line with our mission and enhance the community.

Q: A s you look at your future in the next year ahead, what are some specific things that you would like to accomplish between today and the next 365 days?

Benko: Immediately it's getting out and talking to people. today we had a chance to meet with all the staff and all the head coaches and really digest and then synthesize a lot of information. I will tell you what's front of mind for me is making sure with football with Jimmy, I mean, we've got the '27 signing class offers going out here soon. I had a chance to visit with him yesterday, so it's really good that we're on the same page, but also opportunities to, to re-sign guys and then ultimately the portal. So I gotta make sure we're there. With T.J. and, and, and Bill and the staff on, on their assignees and all our coaches, so it's really right now making sure they have the resources they need to be successful.

I shared with them this morning also too, my job is to remove roadblocks. I'm not gonna have all the answers day one, but I do think it's, it's making sure, meeting them at their venue, learning about their programs, getting in front of all the student-athletes and it's the same thing with donors. I look forward to get on the road and visit all 99 counties. It's gonna take a little bit of time. I look forward to that because, see, to me, I'm energized by people, and I also wanna know that, like what makes Iowa State special, what we may need to make sure we never change, and what are some things that we can enhance. I think that sometimes you have to really get boots on the ground. So I'm not gonna sit here and tell you it's a listening tour for 6 months. There'll be a lot of listening, but there's gonna be decisive action when needed as well.

Every job is different, every opportunity is different. I'm very fortunate and very blessed to come in behind Jamie because he has a great staff. He has a legacy to live on for a long time, and, and we had a, Jamie and I talked on Friday, and he's offered to be of assistance and, and so, you know, I think there's so many great people that want to see Iowa State be successful that, um, it's really a chance to connect that first year with them.

Q: I'm curious, before you were even in the running for this job growing up in this industry, what did you know about Iowa State and maybe what have you learned through this entire process?

Benko: The fan support to me is always, that's synonymous – I've also had, we've had several friends and former coaches, obviously, Alex Golesh, at Auburn and Charlie Henry at Georgia Southern. Both have told me Ames is their, their favorite place they've lived. So to me that carries a lot of weight. The other thing I heard were the fans and donors and the staff want to find every reason to like you. I understand it's not about likability, but it really spoke to just how people in this community come together. So that's what I knew about it. I talked to T.J. about it the other day about the Sweet 16, the Maui, but also seeing them in, in a tournament in the past and, it's amazing when you turn on the TV, both in football, basketball, women's basketball, wrestling, you name it.

To me, the passion is what I'm used to, 365 and my experiences. To me, I just, that really attracts me and really appeals to me. That's really what stuck out. The last piece too is just what a great community. When you look at our research and being an R1 institution and the first land grant institution in the country.

Q: Wondering on facilities that was something that I think was kind of put on the back burner. There was a wrestling facility planned, that was kind of put to the back burner with the rev share NIL kind of coming around. I know that that was one of your focuses at a previous stop was facilities. Where do you kind of see that at Iowa State and anything in particular you'll be taking a look at?

Benko: I think there's, there's no right or wrong answer. I think you want to try to do it all, but not the sacrifice of not doing anything. And so I've got a lot to learn about that facility. I've heard some really unique design on that also, there's some opportunities, I think at Hilton as well. I need to come in and listen and learn and, and take it all into context, cause I think right now for a long time, you could, you know, you go back 5-10 years ago, you really could make facilities a priority. We're gonna continue to make them a priority, but you've got to balance a little more than you did 5, 10 years ago. So, I've got a lot of listening and learning to do when I get, when I get here officially.

articles.title: Report: Ravens re-sign K Jake Moody to practice squad
articles.summary: Jesse Minter did not hide his frustration with Tyler Loop after the kicker missed a 49-yard field goal in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
Jesse Minter did not hide his frustration with Tyler Loop after the kicker missed a 49-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. The Ravens led 10-3 at the time and lost 13-10.

"Confronting issues and confronting problems is really what this whole thing's about ," Minter said Monday, via Clifton Brown of the team website. "There's kicks that take a lead game from a two-score game to a three-score game … or take that from a one-score game to a two-score game. Those are critical misses.

"There's a confidence level for how he prepares and how he practices and operates and strikes the ball. But at the same time, that position itself is completely results driven. We'll continue to work with him and try to put him in position. But we need to make second-half kicks. You could argue that second-half missed field goals are no different than turning the ball over."

Loop has made 10 of 13 field-goal attempts this season, including a walk-off 56-yarder in overtime to beat the Cowboys in Week 3. All three misses have come from 40-49 yards, with only two makes in five attempts from that distance.

The Ravens are signing kicker Jake Moody to their practice squad, bringing him back as competition for Loop.

They previously signed Moody after Loop missed three of his eight field-goal attempts in the preseason. They cut Moody from the practice squad on Sept. 15 after Loop made field goals of 57 and 45 yards against the Colts.

articles.title: Chad Ochocinco willing to pay for Jesse Legree to stay at Oregon State
articles.summary: Former Oregon State star Chad Ochocinco has offered to pay to help keep freshman phenom Jesse Legree with the Beavers.
articles.body:
The wide world of name, image, and likeness has certainly changed the landscape of college athletics, for good and for bad. On one hand, a team like the Oregon State Beavers can't fully appreciate the phenomenal season that true freshman wide receiver Jesse Legree is having, because there are worries that he will potentially take a massive paycheck from a bigger team in the transfer portal this offseason.

However, NIL also lets a wealthy former player—Chad Ochocinco, in this scenario—pony up and try to pay enough to keep Legree in Corvallis.

Earlier this week on his podcast, Ochocinco announced that he was willing to do whatever he could to keep Legree with the Beavers next year, even if that meant putting up $2 million in NIL funds, so long as Oregon State did what it could to match the funds.

"Hey, JaMarcus Shephard, you give him $2 million, I give him $2 million," Johnson said. "That's $4 million right there."

While a $4 million NIL deal may sound like a lot for a true freshman, Legree might be worth it. Through seven games, the first-year Beaver has hauled in 46 passes for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. He has also been named the Pac-12 Freshman of the Week seven weeks in a row.

Watching his ascension from a former 3-star athlete in the 2026 class to what he's become now has been wildly entertaining for Beavers fans, but the impending dread of seeing him potentially leave for a bigger school this offseason looms large.

That is, if Ochocinco doesn't have a say in the matter.
