articles.title: Chargers vs. Chiefs: Good, bad and ugly from LA's 22-6 loss
articles.summary: The Chargers fell to 0-6 after their loss to the Chiefs. Here are the highlights and lowlights from the Week 6 game.
articles.body:
The Chargers failed to pick up their first win of the 2026 season after losing 22-6 to the Chiefs.

To recap Week 6, here is a look at the good, the bad, and the ugly.

Special teams: Special teams coordinator Ryan Ficken's unit had an excellent day. Troy Dye forced a fumble on Chiefs returner Nikko Remigio, Derius Davis looked sharp with a 21-yard punt return, punter JK Scott boomed a 60-yarder to help flip field position, and kicker Cameron Dicker accounted for all of the Chargers' points.

Defensive resistance: Despite the score, the Chargers' defense kept things competitive early, but they were worn down by time of possession and struggles with field position. Overall, Los Angeles held one of the highest-scoring offenses to 1-of-4 in the red zone and 3-of-10 on third-down situations.

Offensive line: Playing without starters Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt, and Kayode Awosika, a patchwork offensive line featuring four rookies was completely overwhelmed. The Chiefs' defensive front harassed Justin Herbert all afternoon, racking up four sacks and consistent pressure.

The 1-yard line collapse: After Quentin Johnston's 57-yard catch on the opening series in the second half, the Chargers had a prime chance to make it a one-score game. Instead, they committed a holding penalty, lost a yard on a shovel pass, threw consecutive incompletions, and managed to walk away with just a field goal.

Ladd McConkey's bad luck: McConkey has dealt with injuries this season, and they continued on Sunday. The injury happened in the first quarter after McConkey caught a 17-yard pass from Herbert and was tackled near midfield by Nohl Williams and Nick Bolton, causing his head to hit the turf, later being identified as a concussion.

Run defense: The Chargers entered the week boasting a top-10 run defense, but running back Kenneth Walker III had his way, shredding them for 128 yards and 2 touchdowns, averaging 6.7 yards per carry and forcing multiple missed tackles.

Offensive output: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's group struggled heavily again, failing to find the end zone. The ground game was completely neutralized, rushing for a measly 73 total yards (3.3 yards per carry). The offense looked completely toothless in the red zone, going 0-for-3 (and 0-for-3 on fourth downs). McDaniel's play-calling lacked confidence despite plenty of opportunities to strike.

Justin Herbert's interception bug: While the environment didn't help him, Herbert threw another inexcusable interception straight to linebacker Jack Cochrane in the second quarter. It marked his third straight game throwing a pick and extended his league-leading total to eight interceptions.

articles.title: Defensive grit a welcome sign for the Cardinals, who showed pride in snapping 4-game skid
articles.summary: (AP) — The Arizona Cardinals are a flawed football team that probably doesn't have enough raw talent to compete for a playoff spot this season.The Cardinals...
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — The Arizona Cardinals are a flawed football team that probably doesn't have enough raw talent to compete for a playoff spot this season.

But they do have some pride. For one week, that was enough.

The Cardinals (2-4) — who entered Sunday's game as 12.5-point underdogs — pulled off a big upset with an 18-16 road win over the Los Angeles Rams. It was a potentially job-saving coaching performance by Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, whose unit had given up 37 points per game during the previous four-game losing streak.

"I thought (Rallis) was excellent today," first-year coach Mike LaFleur said Sunday. "I thought he put them in some incredible spots. I give a lot of credit to that whole defensive staff and then the players making it come to life. It was a really, really good performance by coaches and players on the defensive side."

The Cardinals might have found a recipe for future defensive success with their gameplan against the Rams, dialing up an aggressive approach that featured lots of blitz packages.

Safety Budda Baker and edge rusher Josh Sweat each had a sack and two hits on Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, who rarely looked comfortable in the pocket.

LaFleur — who was the Rams' offensive coordinator for three season before becoming the Cardinals' head coach — knew Rallis' defense had the ability to be better than it showed during the four-game losing streak.

"It's one game. It's a total reset next week. It's a 1-0 league," LaFleur said. "But it's something that I truly feel like we can build on because, again, I've had to go against this defense enough over the years and it's not fun when it's clicking like that."

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett has usually put up good individual statistics during his 18-game tenure as the team's starter, but the Cardinals had a 3-15 record over those contests.

Win No. 3 was particularly sweet because Brissett led the game-winning drive, connecting with Jalen Brooks on a 21-yard catch before the Rams were called for a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty, which put Arizona in field goal range.

The Cardinals have to find a way to get into the end zone instead of kicking field goals. Arizona did a lot of things right on offense, gaining a respectable 338 yards and running 70 plays, which allowed the Cardinals to control time of possession, but the unit was just 5 of 15 in third down conversions.

"It's definitely frustrating, especially playing against a team like that," Brissett said. "At any point they can go score. So, you obviously understand that touchdowns are a premium. We have got to go back and watch the film and get better at that."

Kicker Chad Ryland has had some frustrating misses during his Cardinals tenure, but he was automatic against the Rams, connecting on six field goals from 34, 30, 22, 38, 27 and 43 yards to account for all 18 points. Those are all from a reasonable distance that an NFL kicker should make, but going 6-fot-6 in any game is impressive.

The Cardinals feel like wide receiver Michael Wilson can be a No. 1 option, which is one reason they felt OK about moving on from former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr., trading him to the Texans. But Wilson has been relatively quiet without Harrison on the field, catching eight passes for 62 yards over the two games combined.

Defensive lineman Walter Nolen III had a right ankle injury. LaFleur said he would know more about the severity of the injury later in the week.

2 — Wins for the Cardinals at SoFi Stadium this season. They also beat the Los Angeles Chargers in Inglewood in the season opener.

The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos on Sunday.

articles.title: England coach should be English, suggests Fleming
articles.summary: New Zealander Stephen Fleming, England’s new Test coach, suggests the national team should be led by someone from England.
articles.body:
New Zealander Stephen Fleming, England's new Test coach, has suggested the national team should be led by someone from England.

Fleming, who will take charge of his first series in South Africa in December, is the latest overseas coach to lead the England men's team.

Since 1999, only two Englishmen - Peter Moores (twice) and Chris Silverwood - have been in charge of the Test side, while Ashley Giles had a spell as white-ball coach.

In the same time period England have been led by two Zimbabweans, in Duncan Fletcher and Andy Flower, and Australian Trevor Bayliss - while Fleming has succeeded his fellow Kiwi Brendon McCullum, who remains white-ball coach. Another Australian, Matthew Mott, also had time in charge of the white-ball team.

Fleming's backroom team, announced last week, is heavily weighted towards homegrown coaches.

Former England opener Marcus Trescothick, who was in interim charge of the Test team earlier this year, is joined by ex-England wicketkeeper James Foster and former spinner Richard Dawson.

Jonathan Trott, an Ashes winner with England, is about to begin a spell in charge of England Lions. Both Trott and Dawson were in the running for the Test job before Fleming was appointed.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, former New Zealand captain Fleming said it will be a "priority" of his tenure to help develop English coaches.

"I do believe that primarily the national team should be coached by a national representative," said Fleming.

"I'm grateful for the opportunity, but there will be some development in terms of the coaching, and you can see by our staff."

As well as Fleming and McCullum filling the head coach roles for the men's national teams, England's selector, Marcus North, is Australian.

In September it was announced that another Australian, Leah Poulton, will become the managing director of England women. Between 2020 and 2023 England women's head coach was Lisa Keightley, the former Australia international.

In addition to developing the coaches on his own staff, Fleming said he will also occasionally invite county coaches and former England players into the set-up.

"There are some really key people who have come back into the system and I'm really pleased about that," he said.

"I look forward to working with them, but it is a real focus and it's an ambition as well that you will also get county coaches who will be introduced at certain times and you will get past players that will be asked to come back as well.

"It's really inclusive and a comfortable nature of using what's around, but also driving what should be driven within the county game and the English game."

One of the criticisms of McCullum's four-year spell in charge of the Test team was his lack of time spent around the county game.

In September, Fleming visited some counties and also spoke of his affection for the domestic game in England. The former batter had spells as a player with Nottinghamshire, Yorkshire and Middlesex.

He confirmed he will spend part of next summer watching county cricket in the build-up to the home Ashes series.

"Yep, I'll be around and I really enjoyed this year getting to catch up," said Fleming. "A lot of the guys I played with are now in positions either coaching or the head positions at counties.

"It was good to catch up with those guys and get a feel for where the county game is at. I really enjoyed it and it will be a key part to continuing developing players."

Fleming was appointed in July, though did not take charge for the series against Pakistan in August and September, meaning his first series at the helm will be the three matches in South Africa in December and January.

The squad for that series is due to be named in the first week of November.

England did not pick a specialist spinner in any of the three Tests against Pakistan, instead fielding four frontline seamers.

In South Africa's ongoing Test against Australia in Gqeberha, the tourists have omitted Nathan Lyon despite the off-spinner sitting sixth on the all-time list of Test wicket-takers with 573.

Last week, Shoaib Bashir was named as the only specialist red-ball spinner on England's list of fully centrally contracted players, while Mason Crane and Liam Patterson-White were given development deals.

Following the tour of South Africa, spin will play a big role on the two-Test tour of Bangladesh in February.

Asked if Bashir's contract means he is England's number-one spinner, Fleming said the Derbyshire man represents "continuity".

"I acknowledge there's a raft of spinners just below that, that at times are putting their hand up," said Fleming.

"There is a raft of spinners there and are probably looking for an opportunity, and finding those conditions, it could be Bangladesh, where there could be two or three that will come along.

"The team could look quite different and that's the horses for courses example.

"But Bashir has got some experience and is still very young. There's an aspect of still looking and developing, and trying to find that right combination in the spin department."

articles.title: Utah AD Mark Harlan on ‘College GameDay,’ late kickoffs and more
articles.summary: Utah’s athletic director is excited for ‘remarkable’ opportunity to host ‘GameDay’ for third time in four seasons, but expresses disappointment at number of...
articles.body:
It's an exciting week for the University of Utah.

The No. 10 Utes, one of just six college football teams that are still undefeated, are gearing up for the biggest game of their season so far — a late-night matchup against No. 14 Houston.

Saturday's Utah-Houston clash is one of the premier games on the Week 8 schedule and is one of just two ranked-vs-ranked games on the slate, No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas being the other. Since "College GameDay" already visited Austin this year and Texas lost last week, it made Salt Lake City a no-brainer choice for the traveling pregame show.

The "GameDay" production crew won't have to travel very far to set up shop. After airing live from BYU ahead of the Cougars' win over Notre Dame, "GameDay" will make the short drive up I-15 to set up in Salt Lake City for the third time in four years.

"GameDay," which draws millions of viewers each week, will essentially be a three-hour advertisement for the university and the football program.

"Anytime we get to show off our campus and our student body and everything's great about Salt Lake City, University of Utah, I think it's fantastic for the nation to see," said Utah coach Morgan Scalley

While "GameDay" presents another good opportunity to pitch Utah to the nation, the best pitch for the program won't come on the pregame show, it'll come during the game.

"I think the biggest recruiting tool you have is winning games," Scalley said. "That's the biggest recruiting tool you have. So our players understand that it's all about game day and what they do on the field and the best thing they can do to maximize the "College GameDay" experience is to win."

"... Yes, it can be a lot of fun, but ultimately at the end of the day, it's only fun if you win that game."

Hosting "GameDay" has become old hat for the University of Utah.

Saturday will mark the seventh "GameDay" broadcast from Utah's campus. In 2004, the first time the show originated from Utah, Scalley was a senior safety and ESPN's pregame show kicked off a day that saw Utah close out an 11-0 regular season with a 52-21 pummeling of BYU.

"If you want to know who the first rhino was, it was Steve Fifita. He scored a touchdown in that game as they handed the ball off to him," Scalley said, referring to the defensive tackle's punctuating touchdown in that game.

Two decades later, Scalley is the head coach of Utah and "GameDay" is coming back yet again.

"I really want to thank coach Scalley and this staff and this football team for giving us this incredible opportunity with ESPN 'GameDay' coming in," said Utah athletic director Mark Harlan. "I think it's remarkable. There's not a lot of schools out there that have been able to host three of the last four years. There's some in the Big Ten and SEC would dream of that, but we've got it here at Utah."

Utah has always had a good crowd for the ESPN pregame show, and the expectation is that it'll be a packed background at Presidents Circle on Saturday morning. The show starts at 7 a.m. MDT and runs until 10 a.m. The final hour features Rece Davis, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban and Kirk Herbstreit, along with a to-be-announced guest, selecting the day's games.

The show is free to attend and there will be free parking available.

"GameDay" broadcasting from the state of Utah two weeks in a row speaks volumes to the excellent programs in the Beehive State.

"I think what's going on in the state of Utah in football is remarkable," Harlan said. "That story I imagine is going to be told pretty profoundly. To have two teams here in the top 10 in this era is just incredible. Listen, we all know, I mean, I'm really close with Kalani (Sitake). He's awesome.

"And what Morgan's doing, I mean, it's remarkable. I'm on the CFP (committee), so I'm watching every game, but I certainly have been watching them and watching a lot of other teams. But to see both teams win in this way and be undefeated, it's remarkable."

As exciting as it is for "GameDay" to be in Salt Lake City, it'll make for a long day for Utah fans. Kickoff for Saturday is set for 8:15 p.m. MDT on ESPN.

Saturday will mark the fourth time this season that Utah has been scheduled for an 8:15 p.m. kickoff. Three of those games have come at home, though the Kansas game scheduled for 8:15 p.m. was moved up to 6 p.m. due to forecasted inclement weather.

The Pac-12 built a brand on "after dark" games, but the conference actually had rules about how many late-night games each team could play. In the Big 12, there is no such rule, and as a result, West Coast teams like Utah and BYU bear the brunt of games with late starts.

Harlan acknowledges that the constant late-night starts are a sacrifice by fans.

"I also want to take a moment to just thank our fans. Our fans have been so incredible. I recognize that as happy as I was, quite candidly, about 'GameDay' coming, I was equally as disappointed that we got another night game on ESPN," Harlan said. "I like our record at night and I know our players love playing at night, but I know that is a sacrifice and I just want to acknowledge that."

Harlan has talked to television partners and Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark about spreading out the late-night games.

ESPN and Fox reportedly paid $2.28 billion over six years for the TV rights to the Big 12 Conference, and with that money comes the ability to dictate game times. It's a bit puzzling that ESPN is broadcasting one of the best games of the week at 10:15 p.m. eastern time, but the network is doing what is best for it and making sure there's football on from dawn to dusk.

The conference turned over control of game times to the television networks as part of the billion-dollar deal. As a result, the conference and its members are beholden to the decisions of the network.

"Listen, it's such a tough balance. We came into the conference, we inherited the deal, and so I understand it. In some ways the Pac-12 Conference was a little restrictive for the networks because we used to hear from them. Our biggest financier is ESPN and Fox, and they're great partners. They recognize that this is a lot. This is a lot to have four eight o'clock games," Harlan said.

Harlan said that Utah didn't arrive home from its 8:15 p.m. game against Colorado until 5 a.m. Sunday. Arkansas arrived back at its facility at 8 a.m. Sunday following its game at Utah.

"It's not easy for these young people to turn around and recover and that is a significant issue. We got home at 5 a.m. on Sunday. That stuff matters, but ESPN had the first pick this week and they picked the Utes and that's just where it went," Harlan said.

Harlan is also concerned about the fans having to deal with the late-night games, though it hasn't hurt support. Rice-Eccles Stadium is set for its 100th straight sellout on Saturday and the Utah-Houston game is the most expensive ticket on the college football secondary market this week.

"Listen, we're complaining about something, but what my concern is really is just the fans. Too many of those start to really add up," Harlan said.

For what it's worth, Utah's game next week at Cincinnati is set for a 1:45 p.m. MDT kickoff on ESPN or ESPN2. The Utes return home the following week for what could be one of the most important rivalry games ever against BYU.

"I will say, be ready. The BYU game could very well likely be a six-day selection. So we may not know what's going to happen there down the line for a bit," Harlan said.

Other items of note from Harlan's meeting with the media

On what has impressed him during Scalley's first season as head coach

"I would say everything he's done has been even more than I would've expected and I expected a lot. I think the thing that I really appreciate is the relationships and the culture in the program. Guys doing the right things, guys going to class, really focusing in on what they need to do.

"They've had some on-field adversity that they've just managed their way through. So all of that is really remarkable. Also how he's integrated new staff into the system. I talked to those guys how they say this is one of the greatest places they've ever come and coached. So it's all good. There's going to always be tough moments ahead because it's college football, but I can tell you that with him, I have no worries that we're absolutely headed in a terrific direction."

On Crimson Brand Partners, Utah's new for-profit company created as part of private equity deal

"For CBP, I'm thrilled by the start. This is a journey, multiple-year journey. I think (CBP CEO) Matt Webb and his team have done a great job collaborating with all of us to really, what we said all along, is to create the best possible experience.

"We're trying stuff at football. We'll start seeing that in basketball. Some stuff's working, some stuff doesn't work. That's what you do. You'll see the debut of the new north end zone field suites this weekend. We decided to move it up a week and have some people try it out, see what we learn before the actual folks that bought those seats for the next game.

"Obviously in-game production, quality, they're surveying how they're really talking to fans. I mean, this group is primarily all from NFL, NBA and MLB. They're up to 70 people. We used to have 16 people on it. They've got 70. Quantity is important, but quality too. So we're starting to see a lot of lift on that. Certainly some of the deals they've done have been great."

"We're just going to continue to work with (Crimson Brand Partners). Just so you know, that's a joint university and CBP investment, so it's not $40 million just from them. It's kind of split down the middle in terms of the way we look. We'll continue to work with them just like we're going to work with them on the Huntsman renovation project that we're still chipping away at. It'd be crazy not to because they're coming from a lot of places they've built, a lot of facilities and the jobs they've been into.

"It's a constant collaborative conversation, but it's also starting to have conversations with the Olympic organizers too, right? I mean, it's amazing. It's eight years away, but sometimes it feels like it's 10 minutes away. So as we look at our facilities going forward, we're having multiple conversations to see if we can hit the mark.

"It's always going to be important in Utah. Sports teams that will compete here all the time are the No. 1 priority, but we got to take a good look at everything when we're renovating going forward."

On if Utah has any interest in scheduling Notre Dame

"Well, we'd always be interested, but it's just we're really locked. Not that I don't worry about the phone ringing from Baton Rouge (LSU) to get out of a game or Madison (Wisconsin) or where else, I can go on and on, but the phone's not ringing.

Right now I think with the situation of having to play 10 games (Power Four commissioners are discussing moving to 10 conference games with CFP expansion), to flip from one to another is a challenge. Jeff Rudy still is handling our scheduling and does a great job and he's done a really good job. But this is also something, to your point, is how far in advance do you schedule, right? You don't want to go too far because you might have opportunities that come up, but we're in a good spot."

articles.title: Texas vs UConn basketball: Live updates, highlights as Longhorns and Huskies clash
articles.summary: Texas and UConn's women's basketball teams will participate in a high-profile exhibition game on Monday night. Texas and UConn have both been a Final Four qu...
articles.body:
With the start of the regular season around the corner, the Texas women's basketball team will participate in a high-profile exhibition game.

On Monday, Texas will play an exhibition game against UConn. This exhibition game - which UT coach Vic Schaefer said was scheduled as an NIL benefit for the players of both programs - will feature two of college basketball's top powerhouses. Texas and UConn have both been a Final Four qualifier in each of the past two seasons, and UConn won a national championship in 2025.

This will be the first meeting between the two schools since Texas recorded an 80-68 win Dec. 3, 2023 over UConn in Austin.

Texas will be led by senior forward Madison Booker, a three-time Associated Press All-American, while UConn junior forward Sarah Strong was named the AP's Player of the Year for the 2025-26 season. The Longhorns will open their season at home against Fairleigh Dickinson on Nov. 4. UConn's season opener is set for Nov. 2 against Cornell.

This section will be updated as more information becomes available.

Where: PeoplesBank Arena (Hartford, Conn.)

articles.title: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh provides major injury updates
articles.summary: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh provide injury updates on key players after dropping to 0-6.
articles.body:
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh addressed the media on Monday after dropping to 0-6 in the season.

Harbaugh provided injury updates following the loss, saying that offensive tackle Joe Alt and safety Derwin James are "getting closer to returning."

Harbaugh also added that wide receiver Ladd McConkey and cornerback Deane Leonard are in the concussion protocol.

Other players "getting closer to return" include Brenen Thompson, Kayode Awosika, Donte Jackson, Tre' Harris, and Bud Dupree.

Alt, Awosika, Harris, Jackson, Thompson, Dupree, and James all missed Week 6 with their respective injuries.

As for McConkey, he was cleared for the Chiefs matchup but suffered a concussion on Sunday and was ruled out after the second quarter. The 24-year-old's status is unclear. The good news for the Chargers is they have a bye in Week 7.

Leonard suffered his concussion on Sunday as well. Before exiting the game, he recorded two tackles. In the season, Leonard has recorded nine tackles in four games.

Los Angeles sits with a 0-6 record for the first time since the 2000 season.

articles.title: Yankees could target Brewers All-Star if David Bednar leaves in free agency
articles.summary: The Yankees could lose Bednar in free agency.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees ' bullpen may look totally different in 2027.

Six of their relievers will soon become free agents, including closer David Bednar.

The Yankees can extend him a qualifying offer, which would bring him back to New York for at least one season if he accepts.

Bednar is one of the more consistent closers in baseball, converting 35 of 39 saves this season. It would be a major loss for the Yankees if he decides to sign with another club.

Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller wrote that this will be a huge offseason for New York's bullpen roster construction.

"With David Bednar and darn near every other reliever of note hitting free agency, the Yankees have quite a bit of work to do on their bullpen. The dream target would be Mason Miller, if the Padres are willing to have that conversation," Miller wrote.

He identified Milwaukee Brewers closer Trevor Megill as someone the Yankees should target if they fail to re-sign Bednar.

"But while trading for Devin Williams didn't pan out how they hoped in 2025, going back to Milwaukee for Trevor Megill could be the move. He was an All-Star last year and probably ought to be a three-time reigning All-Star at this point," Miller added.

Megill throws a power fastball and nasty knuckle curve, which helped him punch out 69 batters in 61.2 innings in 2026.

He reaches free agency in 2028, and the Brewers have a history of trading their stars one year before they hit the open market.

Josh Hader and Devin Williams (both traded) were in identical contract situations as Megill.

articles.title: Mike Macdonald calls Zach Charbonnet's return this week "a possibility"
articles.summary: Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet could make his 2026 debut on Sunday.
articles.body:
Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet could make his 2026 debut on Sunday.

"Zach is going to have a full week's worth of reps," Macdonald said, via video from Brian Nemhauser of hawkblogger. "So, that's exciting, and there's a possibility you could see him on Sunday in some capacity."

Charbonnet remains on the reserve/physically unable to perform list after tearing the ACL in his left knee on his fifth carry in the divisional round of the 2025 playoffs. He underwent surgery on Feb. 20.

The Seahawks opened his 21-day return-to-practice window Oct. 1, so the Seahawks will have to return him to the active roster this week to avoid him finishing the season on PUP.

Charbonnet ran for 730 yards and 12 touchdowns on 184 carries in the 2025 regular season, while sharing carries with Kenneth Walker. Walker is now tearing up the league in Kansas City after signing with the Chiefs as a free agent.

articles.title: Phillies could lose coach to rival Mets in full-circle rehire
articles.summary: Kevin Long was the Mets' hitting coach from 2015-17.
articles.body:
Kevin Long was the New York Mets ' hitting coach the last time they won a National League pennant. To get back to the World Series for the first time since 2015, the Mets might turn to Long for a short reboot.

On the same week he was fired by the Philadelphia Phillies , Long scheduled an interview with the Mets about a position on their 2027 coaching staff, according to Mike Puma of the New York Post .

Long was the Mets' hitting coach from 2015-17, between coaching stints with the New York Yankees (2017-14) and Washington Nationals (2018-21).

Coincidentally, the Phillies named Carlos Mendoza their third-base coach and infielders' coach last Thursday, less than four months after he was fired from his job managing the Mets. New York missed the postseason and finished last in the NL East with a 74-88 record this season.

Long, 59, was the Phillies' hitting coach from 2022-26 on Rob Thomson's staff. Thomson was fired in April and replaced on an interim basis with bench coach Don Mattingly. When Mattingly signed a two-year contract to return to the Phillies, Long was not retained.

Long has reached the World Series with four different clubs as hitting coach: the Yankees in 2009, the Mets in 2015, the Nationals in 2019, and the Phillies in 2022.

Although the Phillies haven't been back to the World Series since, the team's lineup had its share of success under Long. Philadelphia slugged 220 home runs in 2023, the second-most for a single season in club history. They also saw six different players hit at least 20 home runs in 2023, a franchise record.

In 2016, the Mets hit a franchise-record 218 home runs under Long. From 2007-14, the Yankees led MLB in home runs (1,584) and RBIs (6,206), and ranked second in runs (6,485).

Ohio State coach Ryan Day said quarterback Julian Sayin is still expected to miss several weeks after he was injured at Indiana .

"They're still going through some of their testing and meetings," Day said during an appearance on the "Buckeye Roundtable" on 97.1 The Fan on Oct. 19.

Day provided no other update on the status of Sayin beyond reiterating the timeline.

Sayin left with an injury during the fourth quarter of the Buckeyes' 19-15 win over the Hoosiers on Oct. 17 and did not return.

When Indiana defensive lineman Mario Landino sacked Sayin on a first down just past midfield, he collided into his arm. The hit sidelined Sayin, who went into the locker room at Memorial Stadium and later emerged with his right arm in a sling.

Day first mentioned that Sayin would miss several weeks during his postgame news conference, indicating there would be a significant change at quarterback.

Sayin has been behind center for the Buckeyes throughout two seasons, making 21 consecutive starts since beating out Lincoln Kienholz in a preseason competition as a redshirt freshman in 2025.

Kienholz spent last season as the backup behind Sayin before he transferred to Louisville, leaving Ohio State with less experience on the depth chart.

Luke Fahey, a freshman from Southern California who replaced Sayin at Indiana, is in line to start after emerging as the backup over Tavien St. Clair, a former five-star recruit from Bellefontaine.

Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X.

articles.title: A new Eastern Buckeye Conference football-only league take shape
articles.summary: After the EBC lost schools within the past year as Stark County-area high school leagues make changes, a new EBC football-only league takes shape.
articles.body:
ALLIANCE — It's the dawn of a new day for what is currently called the Eastern Buckeye Conference .

The conference has announced that Canton Central Catholic and Columbiana Crestview will join current EBC members Alliance, West Branch , Salem and Warren Howland to form a new football-only league starting with the 2028 season.

All six schools recently signed long-term four-year commitments to the new league. The league becomes official pending approval by school boards of the respective member schools. The name of the league, whether it remains the EBC, or a new name is chosen, is to be announced.

Stark County-area high school football. Our best images of 2026

"What's nice is they (Canton Central Catholic and Crestview) come from two different areas, so we kind of broaden (the league footprint) a little bit," said West Branch athletic director Ryan Wolf. "Salem (paired) with Crestview and Alliance with another Stark County team (in Central), helps. For us, we're in the middle (of the league geographically), but what's interesting is we've played Crestview in the past and we used to scrimmaged Canton Central Catholic when I played (at West Branch with coach Jim) Laut, and it was always the first scrimmage. Having that tradition (with Central) is a nice thing, and Crestview — everything they do is good."

The new league development comes only months after original EBC conference members Carrollton, Minerva and Marlington announced their departure for the new Northeast Senate League when their two-year EBC exit commitments end following the 2027 season.

Then, last spring, Salem accepted an invitation to join the Youngstown-based Northeast 8 Athletic Conference in all sports but football, starting with the 2027 scholastic season. The Quakers will be in this new football-only league.

The announcement that Minerva, Carrollton and Marlington were departing initially left the EBC scrambling to keep the league afloat in football. But through the efforts of several athletic directors of current EBC members who re-structured a new league in a short time, the new conference, whether it remains the EBC or has a new title, will remain part of the area football fabric.

"I would say it (making the new league happen) was kind of between (Alliance AD and football coach (Tim) Goodman, myself and (Salem AD) Matt Freeman," said Wolf. "It's been kind of a team effort with Jim Carmichael, the commissioner. He's been involved. It was a team effort, it wasn't one person."

With the addition of Stark County-based Canton Central Catholic and Columbiana County-based Crestview, the league's football footprint remains in four counties, including Stark, Mahoning, Columbiana and Portage County. It also strengthens its presence in the Canton and Youngstown media markets.

The new league includes three schools who have won state football titles in their past — Central Catholic (1988, 2000, 2016), West Branch (1994) and Alliance (big-school state poll title in 1958).

"We're real happy that we were able to keep a lot of us together and to keep it local," said Wolf. "I think that was big for us that we were able to keep some rivalries. Football is definitely the hardest one to schedule of every sport. So, to be able to say, hey, we've got five (league) games that are for sure at the end of the season was kind of a relief in that aspect."

Moving forward, the league's six members will consider applications from additional schools that have shown a possible interest in joining the conference in the future.

"Our play was this: Let's get our six (initial members) settled and then let's look at what it would take to expand (in the future)," stated Wolf. "It was OK, we've got six and we'll see how this looks and then from there we can start looking at what we would do if we wanted to add (schools)."

One thing Wolf stated in closing is that West Branch and Alliance will be a new Week 10 league game starting in 2028. Currently, Alliance plays Marlington and West Branch plays Salem in Week 10, but that will change starting in 2028."Alliance will be Week 10 (for West Branch)," said Wolf. "We haven't really worked through all of that (future scheduling). "Preliminary, we have (Salem) (Week 9)."

articles.title: "It is utter rubbish": David and Victoria Beckham's royal wedding appearance sparked unexpected seating controversy
articles.summary: David and Victoria Beckham found themselves at the centre of an unexpected royal wedding controversy in 2011, just months after attending one of Britain's
articles.body: David and Victoria Beckham found themselves at the centre of an unexpected royal wedding controversy in 2011, just months after attending one of Britain's most celebrated occasions. The couple had joined hundreds of guests at Westminster Abbey to witness Prince William marry Kate Middleton. However, claims about their seating arrangements soon brought unwanted attention to their appearance. Reports suggested the famous couple had been unhappy about their seats at the ceremony. The Beckhams wasted little time in responding, firmly rejecting the allegations and making it clear that they had considered their invitation an honour.David and Victoria Beckham reject royal wedding seating allegationsThe controversy emerged after Lady Elizabeth Anson, a cousin of Queen Elizabeth II who helped organise the royal wedding, discussed the event in NBC's documentary Inside The Royal Wedding. According to her account, the Beckhams were unhappy about being seated towards the back of Westminster Abbey.The suggestion raised questions about whether the celebrity couple had expected more prominent treatment at the high-profile ceremony. David Beckham was already a global football icon, while Victoria Beckham had established herself as a successful singer and fashion figure. Their presence at the wedding had attracted considerable attention, making the claims particularly newsworthy.However, the couple strongly disputed the account. Their representative issued a direct response, saying: "We have never had any dealings with Lady Elizabeth Anson. David and Victoria were honoured to be at the royal wedding and it is utter rubbish to say otherwise."The statement left little room for speculation about their feelings towards the occasion. Rather than allowing the claims to define their experience, the Beckhams reaffirmed their appreciation for being included in the historic celebration.The Beckhams describe Prince William and Kate Middleton's wedding as heartfeltThe couple had also shared their positive reaction to the ceremony on the day of the wedding in April 2011. Their statement described the occasion as "beautiful and heartfelt", reflecting a very different impression from the frustration later attributed to them.Prince William and Kate Middleton married at Westminster Abbey on April 29, 2011, in a ceremony watched by millions around the world. Around 350 guests attended the service, which brought together members of the royal family, public figures and celebrities.The guest list included Sir Elton John, Tara Palmer-Tomkinson and Rowan Atkinson, adding to the event's star power. Yet the attention surrounding the Beckhams demonstrated how even small details from a royal occasion could become major talking points.Looking back at the 2011 controversy, the couple's response remains the clearest public indication of their position. articles.title: WWE Raw Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights From October 19
articles.summary: WWE returned to San Diego for Monday's episode of Raw, headlined by the latest appearance from World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns.
articles.body:
WWE returned to San Diego for Monday's episode of Raw, headlined by the latest appearance from World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns.

What did the Tribal Chief have to say about the latest in the Bloodline vs. 946 rivalry, including the latter's newest member, Carmelo Hayes?

Find out the answer to that and more with this recap of the October 19 Netflix broadcast, including grades and analysis of each of the night's matches and biggest segments.

Triple Threat Match for the Intercontinental Championship: Rey Mysterio vs. Dragon Lee vs. Chad Gable

Sami Zayn and Roman Reigns Kicked Off Raw

Last Time in Action: Sami Zayn defeated Kevin Owens (SmackDown, September 18); Roman Reigns defeated LA Knight (Money in the Bank, October 10)

WWE Champion Sami Zayn, ever desperate to be taken seriously in that role, kicked off Raw and asked the fans in San Diego who was there to "ride or die with the Last Real Good Guy."

World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns, whom Zayn zipped past backstage on his way to the ring, interrupted and entered to a thunderous ovation. Chants of "OTC" greeted him as he entered the ring and came face-to-face with the former "Sami Uso."

"I can't believe I'm saying this, and I might be the only one in here saying it, but it's good to see you," Reigns said. The former Bloodline teammates engaged in a mid-ring embrace before Zayn admitted to getting everything the Tribal Chief preached.

The pleasantries came to an end when Reigns questioned Zayn's motivation for being there and a potential allegiance to 946. Then they verbally battled over which championship was more important. Then, the Last Real Good Guy took exception to the disrespect Reigns has shown him by not even sweating him.

"Knowing your track record, you might not even have that championship come Crown Jewel," Reigns said to close out the segment. As he exited the arena, Penta arrived, a not-so-subtle reminder that the luchador has the Money in the Bank briefcase and, one day, will come for the world championship.

Zayn looked utterly disappointed as Reigns interrupted him, stealing his moment and taking the spotlight from him.

"The disrespect! " Reigns said, echoing the "burden" that Zayn feels as champion.

"There are eight billion people in the world right now and only one is the WWE champion and you're looking at him!" Killer line by Zayn that immediately clapped back at the disrespect shown to him by Reigns.

This was an outstanding segment that played on the past history of the champions, asked which title is more important, hinted that Zayn may have ties to 946, and looked ahead via the Penta arrival. This did everything it needed to and above all, set up the story for Reigns vs. Zayn beyond the two being current world champions.

Last Time in Action: Penta won the namesake ladder match (Money in the Bank, October 10); Bron Breakker lost the namesake ladder match (Money in the Bank, October 10)

Breakker sought revenge and a high-profile win in the opening match of Monday's show, tossing Penta around with a few suplexes and obliterating him with a clothesline.

The Badass attempted to catch Penta on a dive to the arena floor but lost his balance. He recovered nicely, driving his opponent into the announce table as the show went to break.

Penta fought his way back into the match later, but Breakker brought him crashing off the top rope with a wicked Frankensteiner for a two-count. The resilient luchador recovered, fended off interference from Austin Theory, and took to the air, only to suffer a mid-flight spear.

Theory attempted to use the briefcase on the babyface, but Je'Von Evans wiped him out on the floor, then stunned Breakker with the same briefcase, and Penta earned the win with the Mexican Destroyer.

This felt like the sort of match that would have been Breakker's to win, with a chance to keep him hot in the wake of a big performance at Money in the Bank. It was not meant to be, though, as it appears Breakker vs. Evans is the direction instead.

Theory is literally one-half of the tag team champions, the very title that Breakker holds along with him, but is treated like an absolute joke. He is very much the tackling dummy for The Vision, a role that does nothing of any real benefit for him other than guaranteeing him TV time every week.

Chelsea Green and Iyo Sky vs. Roxanne Perez and Raquel Rodriguez

Last Time In Action: Roxanne Perez defeated Chelsea Green (Raw, October 12); Raquel Rodriguez and Perez defeated Sol Ruca and Lola Vice (Raw, October 5); Iyo Sky defeated Lyra Valkyria (Raw, September 28)

WWE Women's Champion Green recruited Sky to be her partner against The Judgment Day's Roxanne Perez and Women's Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez.

The heels weathered the early arsenal of their opponents to seize control through the commercial break. After several minutes cut off from her partner, Sky tagged Green in and the blue brand's top competitor exploded into the match.

Despite late interference from Liv Morgan, Green and Sky earned the win when the former wiped her Crown Jewel opponent and Perez out on the floor while the Genius of the Sky delivered a hurricanrana into a rollup for the win.

Green and Sky defeated Perez and Rodriguez

This was a helluva fun match-up, where Green felt more comfortable than in her singles match a week ago and Sky's established chemistry with her opponents helped elevate the contest's quality.

Perez is at a different level of in-ring performance than we have seen out of her to this point and there is an argument to be made that she was the best wrestler in the squared circle tonight. Even with Sky there.

Last Time in Action: Joe Hendry lost to Ethan Page (Main Event, September 17); JD McDonagh and Dominik Mysterio defeated Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee (Raw, October 5)

Flanked by someone wearing a JD McDonagh Funko Pop head, Joe Hendry battled the Irish Ace in singles competition, the latest chapter in their month-long rivalry.

A competitive match was, unfortunately, overshadowed by the Funko nonsense and the presence of Mysterio at ringside, including a guitar shot from the heel to Hendry's masked friend.

Back inside the squared circle, Hendry looked to be on his way to victory when Mysterio interfered, setting up a devastating headbutt from McDonagh for the win.

McDonagh won a match. It was long overdue for the workhorse of Raw and an immensely talented wrestler who loses far too much. That Hendry essentially loses nothing in return only enhances the effectiveness of booking decision.

Can this please be the end of the Funko chicanery?

Last Time in Action: Lola Vice lost the titular ladder match (Money in the Bank, October 10); Lyra Valkyria lost to Sol Ruca (Main Event, October 14)

The showdown between Vice and Valkyria, the result of an errant shot from the latter backstage, continued the steady string of in-ring action.

Valkyria dominated entering the break, targeting the back of her opponent just nine days removed from Money in the Bank.

Vice caught Valkyria coming off the ropes with a wicked spinning heel kick. The heel responded with a nasty baseball slide-style kick that stunned Vice.

On the floor, an unknown assailant grabbed hold of Valkyria's foot. Moments later, Bayley revealed herself to be the attacker, with the distraction allowing Vice to score the win with the MIA backfist.

After the match, the fight between Bayley and Valkyria continued, leading to The Role Model issuing a challenge for a match next week.

Vice is one wrestler who has experienced little-to-no issues making the jump from NXT to the main roster. She has enjoyed a rather seamless call-up and just delivered a strong performance against one of the best wrestlers on the main roster women's division.

The Bayley vs. Valkyria No Disqualifications Match on next week's show should bring an end to their rivalry and, hopefully, allow both women to move on to bigger and better after what feels like an infinitely long rivalry.

Intercontinental Championship Match: Rey Mysterio vs. Dragon Lee vs. Chad Gable

Last Time in Action: Rey Mysterio defeated Big Cass (Raw, October 12); Dragon Lee lost to Austin Theory (Main Event, October 14); Chad Gable defeated Rey Fenix (Raw, October 12)

Live from his hometown of San Diego, Rey Mysterio challenged Chad Gable for the Intercontinental Championship in a match also involving the 2023 Hall of Famer's protege, Dragon Lee.

As he has in the face of challengers since dethroning Penta back at SummerSlam, Gable withstood the flurry of offense thrown at him by his opponents and emerged victoriously, rolling Mysterio up for the grueling victory.

After the match, as the all-time-great competitor showed Gable respect, Ethan Page and Big Cass attacked out of nowhere. All Ego focused on Gable, laying him out and posing with the gold, while Cass obliterated Lee with a chokeslam on the guardrail.

To the surprise of absolutely no one, this match ruled.

It was helped exponentially by the crowd's red-hot reaction to their hometown hero and how close he came to winning the IC title. This was his best performance in a while.

Page got great heel heat here by way of his attack on the victory and Mysterio. All Ego was phenomenal upon his arrival earlier this year. Hopefully, this is a sign of more important things to come.

The pissed-off Usos hit the ring for the main event segment of the night and wasted no time calling out 946.

Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Lucien Prince, and Bronco Nima answered, led to the ring by Jaida Parker.

Solo Sikoa attacked from behind and the siblings had momentum until Hayes delivered a crowbar attack to the knee. The heel faction proceeded to beat down The Usos and Sikoa, with Keys overheard telling Sikoa, "Tell Roman," only for the OTC to arrive on the scene.

Reigns joined his Bloodline in fending off the heels and stood tall to close the show.

The only way this could have been better was if William Regal himself trotted to the ring and uttered "War Games!"

This has been the clear direction for months but the arrival of Reigns and his subsequent beatdown of Keys and Co. elevated this segment and, suddenly, this entire rivalry tenfold.

If WWE protects him enough, Keys can be a legitimate challenger to Reigns' title coming out of this.

From his opening promo with Sami Zayn to his late-show heroics alongside his family, this was a Reigns-heavy show. He delivered, too, delivering a great verbal performance with Zayn before whopping up on the 946 in the closing segment to set up what feels like War Games.

More motivated than ever this year. Reigns' record has been nothing short of extraordinary. Great stuff from the OTC in what feels like a revenge tour against all critics.

This was another strong episode of Raw, bogged down only by the Hendry-McDonagh match that was more about the bobblehead mascot at ringside than anything.

Otherwise, good wrestling, strong angles, and some great planting of seeds helped establish this as one of the better episodes of Raw in some time.

articles.title: Rays beat Guardians to book a World Series showdown with the Brewers
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays are headed to the World Series for the third time in franchise history, booking a Fall Classic showdown with the Milwaukee Brewers.
articles.body: The Tampa Bay Rays are headed to the World Series for the third time in franchise history, booking a Fall Classic showdown with the Milwaukee Brewers. The matchup between the Rays and Brewers pits the two best teams during baseball’s regular season against one another for a title. It also ensures history will be made – neither franchise has ever won a World Series. The Rays punched their ticket to baseball’s biggest stage with a 7-3 victory over the Cleveland Guardians in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series, taking the best-of-seven series four games to two. “I’m very happy for this team right here, for this city. Going to the world series, my God. Unbelievable. I want to cry right now because we put in a lot of work as a team and we did it to support the city,” said star third baseman Junior Caminero to the TBS broadcast. As the interview started to be piped through the stadium’s loudspeakers, Caminero grew even more excited, saying, “I’m very happy. Hey, we played really hard for this city. Tampa is the best, Tampa gave me the opportunity to play here. Tampa is the best. Tampa! This is for you!” The crowd at the suddenly raucous Tropicana Field, one of baseball’s quietest venues during most regular season contests, roared in approval. The Rays got on the board early when second baseman Richie Palacios laced a double into the gap in right-centerfield, scoring Victor Mesa Jr. and Chandler Simpson. Jonny DeLuca’s sacrifice fly in the next inning gave the Rays a 3-0 lead, and Tropicana Field was rocking. The Guardians pulled a run back in the sixth when Nathaniel Lowe knocked a single up the middle, scoring Chase DeLauter. But the moment of the game was to come an inning later when the Rays’ star stepped to the plate. Caminero, a player who would be a major star in the league if he played in almost any other market, walked to the plate after catcher Liam Hicks drew a walk. Caminero hit 42 home runs during the regular season and is one of the few power threats in the small-ball Rays’ lineup. On the first pitch, he turned on a split-fingered fastball that ran toward his hands. Showing off his bat speed, Caminero turned on the ball and pulled it down the left field line. It clanged off the foul pole for a two-run home run that ultimately provided far more than just insurance. In the top of the eighth, the Guardians made their push. DeLauter reached on an infield single and Lowe moved him up with a two-out single of his own. Then the Rays’ bullpen, usually so reliable, turned shaky. Ian Seymour entered to pitch to rookie star Travis Bazzana and walked him to load the bases. Catcher Patrick Bailey then walked to force in a run and Seymour plunked Angel Martinez to force in another. With the wheels threatening to come off, Rays manager Kevin Cash yanked Seymour and put in Kevin Kelly. Kelly righted the ship, striking out Brayan Rocchio to end the Cleveland threat. Just a few moments later, all the worries were set aside for Rays fans. After Taylor Walls earned a one-out walk, longtime Ray Yandy Díaz stepped to the plate. He took a pitch from Cleveland reliever Hunter Gaddis and turned on it, blasting it over the left field fence and sending the Tropicana Field crowd into delirium. It’s a validating moment for an organization known as one of the best front offices in MLB, which has figured out a way using cutting-edge analytics to put together a consistently contending team despite a tight budget. The Rays had a $98.3 million payroll in 2026, ranked 25th in the league. “We’ve got the best baseball organization in the world … this entire organization works tirelessly to put the best team on the field to compete every day, in and out,” said Patrick Zalupski, the team’s principal owner and managing partner. Added Cash: “They’ve been incredible all season long. All of the fans who come into this ballpark, they’ve seen it. We’ve known it and they just went out and proved it this month.” Pitcher Freddy Peralta, who won his two starts in Game 2 and Game 6 and also came in to get some key outs in Game 4 on Saturday, was named ALCS MVP. Peralta will now start in the World Series against his former team in Milwaukee – he played for eight seasons as a Brewer before being traded to the New York Mets ahead of the 2026 season. The Mets dealt him to the Rays at the trade deadline just a few months ago, leading to the serendipitous matchup. It’s the third time that the Rays will play for a title after losing in 2008 to the Philadelphia Phillies and in the Covid-19 shortened 2020 season to the Los Angeles Dodgers. Their opponents, the Brewers, are returning to the Fall Classic for the first time since 1982. The first game of the Fall Classic will be played at 8 p.m. ET on Friday at American Family Field in Milwaukee.

articles.title: Angel Reese scores 30 as Dream stun Valkyries to go level in WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream defeat Golden State Valkyries 79-65 to tie the best-of-seven WNBA Finals at 1-1.
articles.body:
Angel Reese scored 30 points and had 16 rebounds as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries in a stunning win in the WNBA Finals to level the series 1-1 in San Francisco.

Allisha Gray added 18 points as the Dream took full control at both ends in the second half, winning 79-65 on Monday night to even the best-of-seven series before it heads to Atlanta.

Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals, while Jordin Canada contributed 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds as the Dream earned the franchise’s first Finals victory after going winless in three previous trips. They now head home, having salvaged a split in front of the boisterous “Ballhalla” crowd at Chase Center.

“This environment is tough to play in. Shoutout to the fans. Shoutout to my team, though,” Reese said after the game. “We came and fought. I mean, that Game 1 was tough for us. But we moved on.”

Reese became the third player with at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game, joining Jonquel Jones of Connecticut in 2019 and Breanna Stewart of Seattle in 2020.

“She was definitely way more aggressive; she had a great game,” Valkyries centre Kiah Stokes said. “We let everyone kind of have their way.”

Game 3 is Wednesday in Atlanta, where the next two games were moved to the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks’ State Farm Arena so more fans could attend.

It holds more than 17,000, as opposed to the Dream’s regular home, Gateway Center Arena, which accommodates only 3,500.

Chase Center holds 18,064 and has sold out every game since the Valkyries began playing last year.

Gabby Williams finished with 14 points on 3-for-15 shooting after she was the only Golden State player to score in double figures with 26 points in Game 1, going 7 for 24 from the 3-point range.

“We shot terribly,” point guard Veronica Burton said. “We missed shots that we make all the time.”

Foul trouble almost did in the Dream this time, but Reese simply would not have it. She went scoreless in the second half of the opener, but delivered the big baskets and key defensive stops two days later, finishing 10 for 16 from the floor while dishing out three assists and blocking two shots.

“We watched film and saw the things that we messed up on. When I said that they didn’t do anything to mess us up, it was literally just us,” Reese said.

“And we can see that tonight. And we’re gonna carry that over in Atlanta. Atlanta, y’all better pull up and pop out; I’m looking forward to it.”

Atlanta scored 24 points off Golden State’s 19 turnovers to hand the Valkyries their first loss in regulation since a 73-70 defeat at Chicago on August 21.

The Dream had just eight points off turnovers in Game 1, but returned to the defensive formula that advanced Atlanta this far.

articles.summary: Sami Zayn retained the WWE Championship in a DQ loss to Cody Rhodes in a dark match following Monday night's episode of Raw.
articles.body:
Sami Zayn retained the WWE Championship in a DQ loss to Cody Rhodes in a dark match following Monday night's episode of Raw.

Monday's bout was significant in terms of the impact it could have had on what may be the main event of the Crown Jewel premium live event on Nov. 7.

Debating Triple H's Obsession With WarGames Match 👨‍⚖️

WWE already announced that Zayn would face Roman Reigns in a champion vs. champion match at Crown Jewel, and the two faced off in a tense moment during Raw:

Rhodes had a chance to throw a wrench into those plans, however.

Adding even more intrigue to the match is the fact that there was plenty of history between Zayn and Rhodes going into it.

When Zayn became WWE champion for the first time back in June at Night of Champions, he won it from Rhodes in a Triple Threat that also included Gunther.

While Zayn and Rhodes were once friends, that changed in the weeks prior to that match, as Sami proved he was willing to do whatever it took in order to become a world champion.

Zayn dropped the WWE Championship to CM Punk in his first title defense just days later, although that match was originally supposed to be Zayn vs. Rhodes before Cody got attacked backstage.

On the Sept. 11 episode of SmackDown in Mexico, Zayn won the WWE title back from Punk, and he subsequently retained it in a title defense against Kevin Owens one week later.

After being robbed of his WWE Championship rematch about four months ago, Rhodes finally got it on Monday night against the man who beat him for the title in the first place.

Zayn managed to retain, though, likely cementing his Crown Jewel match against Reigns.

articles.title: Patriots Rookie Caleb Lomu Graded by PFF For Two Games as Injury Substitute
articles.summary: The injuries are hitting new levels for the New England Patriots. That includes at offensive line, where the Patriots have been thin all season long.Monday’s...
articles.body:
The injuries are hitting new levels for the New England Patriots. That includes at offensive line, where the Patriots have been thin all season long.

Monday's injury report listed a total of five offensive linemen. That doesn't include Greg Van Roten and Mike Onwenu, who are also on IR right now. Things could be worse, too, with Will Campbell avoiding a major injury after exiting the Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders early.

When Campbell went down, it forced first-round rookie Caleb Lomu into early action. He lived up to the task and seemed like he'd be forced to take over at left tackle until Campbell made his quick recovery. From there, it was back to his backup role. That is, until injuries started pouring in during Week 6.

Three linemen went down in Week 6. That included Morgan Moses, Alijah Vera-Tucker, and Ben Brown. It was Moses' injury that forced Lomu back into action again, this time on the right side of the offensive line. For a second week in a row, he lived up to expectations and more.

New England Patriots Rookie Caleb Lomu Graded by PFF

When the Patriots drafted Lomu, he was seen as a high-upside but raw tackle. So, the hope was to give him 2026 off, maybe bringing him in as a sixth offensive lineman or for the occasional work to adjust to the speed of the game. Then, with time to develop, he could move from left tackle to right tackle to eventually replace Moses.

Injuries aren't letting that happen. However, for anyone watching Lomu play, they'd have to be excited with how well he's playing. Even PFF has noticed that over the past couple of weeks.

In the past two weeks, when Lomu played extensively due to injuries at each tackle position, Lomu has seen 59 pass snaps. He didn't allow a single sack or a single quarterback hit during that time. He's only allowed one quarterback hurry and one total pressure. Drake Maye has to love that.

PFF ranked that as a 99.0 for Pass Block Efficiency. In total, that's also an 80.3 Pass Block Grade.

PFF grades are on a 0-100 scale. That comes from a play-by-play breakdown, where players are graded on a -2 to +2 scale. A 0 grade for a player is a neutral or expected outcome. 60 ends up being an average grade by PFF standards.

Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Praised Caleb Lomu

On Monday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was asked about Caleb Lomu. In particular, how he's developed early in his rookie season.

"Just trying to get ready each and every week," Vrabel said . "It's a lot of new things for him. It's a new league for him. Coming from college, being 21, and it's a tough position to be able to go out there and play. I think he's gotten better. I think that's the goal, to continue to invest in the young guys, coach them and know that that's going to pay dividends down the road."

Down the road has come a lot sooner than they previously expected it to be. Still, he has stood up to a couple of tough tests so far, even if Vrabel is right and the Patriots rookie does have room to grow and improve.

Now, the Patriots are on a short week. It isn't clear if Lomu will be forced into a starting role due to injuries or not. However, he's clearly proven that he's ready when his number does get called.

articles.title: Rays join Brewers in 2026 World Series after ALCS win vs. Guardians
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays are back in the World Series! After six years, Tampa Bay will be playing in the final series of the MLB season. They advanced by beating t...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays are back in the World Series! After six years, Tampa Bay will be playing in the final series of the MLB season. They advanced by beating the Cleveland Guardians in six games in the American League Championship Series. Now, the Rays will take on the Milwaukee Brewers for the championship this season.

The Rays are advancing to the World Series after a dominant 7-3 win in Game 6 of the ALCS against the Guardians. Tampa Bay opened up the scoring in the second inning after a two-run knock by Richie Palacios, and they never looked back from that. They scored one more run in the third inning before Cleveland scored its first run in the sixth inning.

The Guardians were on the verge of mounting a comeback after scoring two runs on Tyler Wells at the top of the eighth inning. However, the Rays scored two more insurance runs in the bottom of that same inning off a Yandy Diaz home run, sealing the deal for Tampa Bay.

The Rays last appeared in the World Series back in 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic. Back then, Tampa Bay faced the Los Angeles Dodgers. At the time, fans weren't allowed to attend games in person. The Rays lost that series 4-2. Now, the fans will be able to wholeheartedly cheer for their team in person as they look to win their first World Series in franchise history.

This time around, the Rays will take on the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series. Milwaukee has been dominant this postseason, dismantling the defending champions Dodgers in a four-game sweep. Milwaukee will have the advantage of longer rest against Tampa Bay… but Tampa Bay's momentum could help them overcome this disadvantage.

articles.title: ‘(Angel) Reese Is a Dawg,’ ‘They Will Never Learn’ — Dream Star Makes a Statement With ‘Cold’ Trash Talk, Block vs. Valkyries Center
articles.summary: Angel Reese did not back down against the Golden State Valkyries’ Aminata Gueye. In a first-quarter sequence in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals, the Atlanta Dream...
articles.body:
Angel Reese did not back down against the Golden State Valkyries' Aminata Gueye. In a first-quarter sequence in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals, the Atlanta Dream star chirped at the French center before blocking her shot on the next possession.

Reese's competitive flair and defensive prowess went viral, earning her high praise on social media.

Angel Reese Turns Heads After Trash-Talking and Shutting Down Aminata Gueye

Down 1-0 in the series, Atlanta needed a win in Monday's Game 2 clash. Reese knew her team couldn't go down 2-0 in the Finals, so she came out swinging to tie the series.

From the opening tip, her intensity was on full display, setting up a viral moment at Gueye's expense.

With just a little over a minute left in the first quarter, Reese was fouled on a shot attempt by Gueye. Between her free throws, the Dream star could be seen talking trash to the Valkyries center.

"You can't [expletive] with me, bum [expletive]," Reese appeared to say before sinking her second shot at the charity stripe.

On the next possession, the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year showed why she earned that award by rejecting Gueye's shot attempt, with Legion Hoops dubbing the sequence "cold."

Fans on social media praised Reese for backing up her strong words.

"Reese is a dawg, sad her teammates can't match her energy," one X user said.

"And then she blocked ole girl at the other end 😂😂😂😂😂😂😂 perfect back up to the [expletive] talk," another commented .

"She exactly who she think she is," one user chimed in .

"I will never tolerate Angel Reese hate/disrespect," a fan declared .

"It's levels in this game," a comment read .

"They will never learn about Angel 😂😂," another posted .

Reese went on to have an impressive outing, earning her first-ever WNBA Finals win. Her two-way dominance helped her squad take over in the second half en route to a 79-65 victory.

She recorded a game-high 30 points on 10-for-16 shooting, knocking down her lone 3-point attempt. Additionally, she led all players with 16 rebounds. Along with her block on Gueye, she rejected Tiffany Hayes in the third quarter for a total of 2 swats.

With the series now tied at 1-1, the Dream have a chance to seize momentum from the Valkyries.

Atlanta will have home-court advantage for the next two games, scheduled for Wednesday and Saturday. Winning both won't guarantee a championship, but it would give the Dream a massive advantage.

Reese also has a chance to make history if she leads her team to the title. She could win a championship in her first Finals appearance while helping the Dream capture their first title in franchise history.

articles.title: Washington Commanders Week 6 Player of the Game: LB Sonny Styles
articles.summary: Commanders' first-round rookie Sonny Styles is Washington's Player of the Game in their 23-17 loss against the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body:
It was a tale of two halves as the Washington Commanders faced the San Francisco 49ers in their first primetime game of the season. Washington couldn't get anything going in the first half, but quarterback Jayden Daniels found the passing game in the second half, giving Washington a chance to win.

The Commanders ultimately lost to the 49ers after Daniels was sacked on the final play. But the defense played a huge role in keeping Washington in the game, holding San Francisco to just three points in the second half. While many players had strong performances in the second half for the Commanders, rookie linebacker Sonny Styles is the player of the game.

Washington drafted Sonny Styles No. 7 overall in April, and he has brought a new mentality to the defense in just a few months. Through the first five games, he was tied for second on the team in total tackles with 33. He was also tied for first on the Commanders in tackles for loss with three.

In this game, Styles led Washington with 13 tackles, marking his second straight game with double-digit tackles. He also had seven solo tackles, his career-high thus far. Styles also defended a pass, his fourth of the season.

Watching this game, it felt like Styles was everywhere for the Commanders' defense, even if he didn't always get the tackle. It is hard to find many rookies in the NFL playing better than him right now, and he will be a key part of Washington's defense for years to come.

Washington will play its next game against the Philadelphia Eagles, who Styles recorded his first career sack against in the season opener.

The San Francisco 49ers held off a late charge from the Washington Commanders to extend their unbeaten start to the season to six games.

The 49ers threatened to run away with it after taking a 20-3 lead into half-time, but Jayden Daniels' touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs late in the third quarter kept Washington's hopes alive.

San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy finished with a touchdown and 264 passing yards, while running back Christian McCaffrey also found the end zone twice.

articles.title: Oregon's Gage Hurych crowned Big Ten Special Teams Player of the Week
articles.summary: Oregon kicker Gage Hurych nailed three field goals against Nebraska and earned Big Ten recognition.
articles.body:
The special teams unit has been one of the biggest and best surprises of the season for the Oregon Ducks , and it certainly played a big role in Oregon's 17-14 win over Nebraska on Saturday. Whether it was flipping the field position and slowly starting the comeback with field goals, the Ducks ' special unit lived up to its name.

Oregon's junior kicker Gage Hurych , in his first season as the Ducks' starting kicker, was named Big Ten Special Teams Player of the Week after connecting on three field goals in the win against Nebraska. Hurych made a pair of kicks from 36 yards and another from 37 yards, all in the second half.

The Ducks have not needed to rely on Hurych for many kicks this season, but when Dan Lanning has called his number, the West Linn product has delivered. Hurych is a perfect 9-for-9 on field goal attempts this season, with a long of 44 yards in the season opener against Boise State , as well as 19-for-19 on extra points. He is one of just seven kickers in FBS who have not missed a field goal this season with at least nine attempts.

Hurych is the first Oregon player to win Big Ten weekly honors this season. Atticus Sappington was the last Oregon specialist to win this award, doing so last November by connecting on three field goals and the game-winning field goal on the road at Iowa.

Hurych will get a chance to build upon his impressive first season as the Ducks' kicker this Saturday, when Oregon travels to Illinois for another Big Ten matchup. Kickoff is set for noon PT with the game airing live on Big Ten Network on Oct. 24.
